## 2026-11-15 — executor — B417 Runtime: weapons and turret

**What**
- `registry/projectile/Projectiles` (new): the projectile choice and creation shared by mobs and vehicles. `Kind` (`ARROW`, `THROWABLE`, `ITEM`, `NONE`), `kind(id)`, `reportOnce(id, who, what, result)`, `forMob` (the mob's shot exactly as before: `ProjectileUtil.getMobArrow`, a throwable at the eyes, a projectile item a little below them), `at` (owned by a player, starting at a point such as a muzzle: `ArrowItem.createArrow` with a bow as the weapon, a throwable, a projectile item), `launch` (the item's own `shoot`, else `Projectile.shoot`). `MobRanged` now uses it; `MobRanged.kind` and the `MobRanged.Projectiles` enum stay as names for the mob GameTests, which are untouched and green.
- `VehicleWeapons` (B412's hooks filled): a `KeyBinds.KeyListener` (registered once when the class loads) fires, on a press of the runtime key `fire` or `second`, every weapon on that key in the presser's seat list (`weaponsOfSeat`) that is ready; `tick` fires `automatic` weapons again each time their cooldown ends while a player in their seat holds the key (`HeldKeys.isHeld`). `fireWeapon(level, index, shooter)`: projectile from the muzzle with the shooter as owner, along the aim at `speed` and `inaccuracy`, then `per_shot` rounds used, `readyAt = gameTime + cooldown_ticks`, `sound` from the server, `recoil` (horizontal push against the shot, sent with `markHurt`), `on_fire` (self the vehicle, player the shooter). `load`: using a weapon's `ammo.item` loads as many as fit from the stack into the first weapon of that ammunition with room (creative stacks are not used up and fill it); a full weapon passes the click on. `aim`, `muzzle` and `ready` are public for B418 and B421.
- `VehicleTurret`: each server tick the turret turns towards the look of the player in `turret.seat` (yaw relative to the hull within `yaw_limit`, pitch within `pitch_limit`, or 0 without `pitch_bone`), at most `turn_rate` a tick; nobody in the seat keeps it where it is. Pure steps `stepYaw` and `stepPitch` for B418's local turret; `gunner()`.
- Test definitions `msm_test:vh_gunship` (two seats with their own weapon lists, a turret with limits, a shell cannon with ammunition, recoil and `on_fire`, an automatic arrow gun on `second`, a snowball gun using 2 per shot) and `msm_test:vh_shell` (a throwable whose `on_hit_block` runs `explode`, breaking blocks).
- `MsmVehicleWeaponGameTest` 8 (replacing the placeholder): seat weapon lists and keys (also the default list), ammunition loading and use (capacity, per shot, endless, creative, full passes on), the cooldown and the dashboard's reload (`readyAt - gameTime`), automatic fire while held, the projectile's owner, start point and aim on the hull and on the turned barrel, recoil, a shell's `on_hit_block` with `explode`, turret limits, turn rate and the hull not turning the aim, the pure steps. 600 GameTests per variant, all green on 26.3, `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib`; JUnit 950. `./gradlew -p parity build` green; parity sample creatures 12 (archer, glider, boss) and sample mob 10 pass on the 26.3 content jar.

**Decisions**
- `muzzle.offset` counts from the vehicle's position (as the templates write it), not from the bone's pivot, which the server does not know: the offset is pitched about a point on the vehicle's upright axis at the muzzle's own height, then turned by the aim's yaw. A muzzle on `pitch_bone` aims with the turret's yaw and pitch, one on `turret.bone` with its yaw only, any other (or none) along the hull's yaw and pitch. No muzzle: the front of the hitbox at half its height.
- `damage` sets an arrow's base damage only, as `msm:ranged_attack`; a throwable's damage is its own. Arrows of a weapon without `ammo` are picked up in creative only (no free arrows).
- The weapon sound plays from the server to everyone, the shooter included, until B418's client plays it at once for the shooter. The shot does not add the vehicle's speed.
- A vehicle weapon whose projectile shoots nothing logs one error per projectile id and weapon field (`weapons[i]`); `msm:ranged_attack` keeps one error per id.
- `Mth.clamp` is gone on 26.4; the turret uses `Math.clamp`.

**Next**
- B418: `VehicleTurret.stepYaw/stepPitch` and `VehicleWeapons.aim/muzzle` for the local turret and the muzzle flash; switch the weapon sound to `playSound(shooter, ...)` once the shooter's client plays it. Recoil on a driven vehicle depends on the driver's client taking the server's motion packet: check it in the client GameTest.
- B421: `fireWeapon` needs a player as shooter; scripts firing without one need an owner rule.

**Decisions**
- The menu is refused any click once it is no longer valid, not only closed at the next tick, so a packet arriving in the same tick as a drop cannot change an orphaned stack.

- `ItemRef.contents` is left for B455 (ADR 0095 D5; B455 owns `ItemRef`).

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B418 Runtime: vehicle client

**What**
- `client/vehicle/MsmVehicleRenderer` replaces B412's `NoopRenderer` placeholder for every vehicle type (one provider instance per type, through the `EntityRendererRegistration` seam of both versions). It bakes `model.geometry` with ADR 0072's `GeoModelBaker`, plays the `idle` and `moving` loops of `model.animations` (clips named `idle`/`moving` or ending in `.idle`/`.moving`) through `GeoAnimationBaker`, draws the hull turned by its yaw and pitch at `model.scale`, the paint's texture from `DATA_PAINT`, and the hurt wobble (`sin(t) · t · share of health lost · 4 · hurt direction` degrees about the hull's length). A missing or broken file draws nothing and is logged once. Never GeckoLib: the same picture on 26.3, 26.4 and without GeckoLib.
- `VehicleModel` turns the named bones each frame on top of the loop: `parts.wheels` roll by the distance travelled over `wheel_radius`, `parts.steering` turn up to 30 degrees, `parts.rotors` spin upright and `parts.propellers` about the forward axis by throttle, `turret.bone` by the turret yaw and `pitch_bone` by its pitch. Model space is the mobs' (front towards -z).
- `VehicleClient` (rewritten): registers the renderers and, each client tick, keeps every vehicle's `Motion` (wheel, steering, rotor, propeller and synched turret angles, this tick's and the last, for interpolation), the engine loop and the exhaust. Throttle and steering come from `DATA_THROTTLE`/`DATA_STEERING`, or on the driver's client from its own `movement().last()`.
- `EngineSound`: `engine.sound` loops at the vehicle while it has a driver and fuel; pitch 0.6 to 1.4 and volume 0.35 to 1 by effort (the larger of the throttle and speed over `max_speed`). `VehicleExhaust`: `exhaust.particle` at `exhaust.offset` every `every_ticks` while the engine works.
- `LocalTurret`: the gunner's client turns the turret towards its own look each tick with `VehicleTurret.stepYaw/stepPitch` and draws that; other clients draw the synched angles interpolated.
- `VehicleInput`: the movement keys reach the physics (`VehicleDriver.clientInput`); a press of fire or second weapon (or holding it for an automatic weapon) that looks ready from the synched cooldown and ammunition plays the weapon sound and a muzzle flash (flame and smoke at `VehicleWeapons.muzzle` of the local aim) at once on the shooter's client. The server's answer (`DATA_READY_AT` moving on) flashes the muzzle on every other client and plays a shot the shooter's client did not predict (a tap shorter than a tick).
- `VehicleWeapons.fireWeapon`: the weapon sound is now `playSound(shooter, ...)`, everyone but the shooter.
- Test assets: `msm_test:vh_car` (engine sound, exhaust, wheels, steering, rotor, a paint, camera 6, animations), `vh_body.animation.json` (an `idle` and an `animation.vh_body.moving` clip), `textures/entity/vh_paint.png` (made here, red check), and `vh_body.geo.json` turned round so its barrel points forwards (-z, as mobs).
- `MsmVehicleClientGameTest` (replacing the placeholder), on a dedicated server, both versions: every vehicle type draws with `MsmVehicleRenderer` and its model has cubes and the named bones; paint swaps the texture; a hit wobbles the hull; driving the car (forward, then right) moves and turns it on the server, rolls the wheels, turns the steering, raises the engine pitch above idle, makes exhaust and holds the third-person camera at `camera.distance` (6, back to 4 after getting out, when the engine loop stops); in the gunship the local and the server's turret reach 60 degrees right and 20 up and stop at the 90-degree limit; the fire key is predicted at once (sound and flash), the server fires a projectile owned by the player, and the cannon's recoil pushes the driver-moved gunship back. Screenshots `msm_vehicle_ingame`, `msm_vehicle_driving`, `msm_vehicle_dashboard`.
- Checked: `./gradlew build` on 26.3, `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib` (609 GameTests each, JUnit 974), `runClientGameTest` on 26.3 and 26.4, `./gradlew -p parity build`.

**Decisions**
- Recoil needs no client code: the server's motion packet reaches the vehicle on its driver's client (checked in the client GameTest on both versions).
- The camera needs no client code: the server's transient `camera_distance` modifier reaches the seated player's client (B406 S5); the test measures it standing still, as a moving frame's camera and the tick's eye position differ by a step.
- The wobble scales with the share of health lost, so vehicles of any `health.max` wobble as a boat at 40 damage would when nearly wrecked.
- `Mth.clamp` is gone on 26.4; the client uses `Math.clamp`.

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B454 runtime: commands and creative tabs

**What**
- Commands (ADR 0096 D1): `loader/CommandParser` (closed `Command` and `Argument` records, `ArgumentType` with the twelve kinds; names, aliases and argument names `[a-z0-9_]`, unique argument names, optionals last, `text` last and `min` not above `max` are errors that refuse the command; a repeated alias and `min`/`max` on a non-number are warnings; events decode one by one, `play_animation` dropped with a warning). `commands/MsmCommands` registers one Brigadier tree per literal through `CommandRegistrationCallback` (every start and every `/reload`) and sends the trees to every player at `END_DATA_PACK_RELOAD`; `CommandBuilder` builds the tree (permission through `Commands.hasPermission(LEVEL_*)`, every node from the last required argument on runs); `CommandArguments` maps the kinds to Brigadier types as `TargetFacts.commands.argumentTypes` and writes the macro values exactly as the eject's `ModCommands`. Running: arguments, then `function <id> with storage <mod id>:args` with `GAMEMASTER`, then the `event` (the source entity as self and other, at the source's position), then `CommandEvents.fire(id, argsJson)`, then `feedback`.
- A literal taken by an earlier project command is a load error at start (the first in scan order keeps it); a literal the dispatcher already has (vanilla or another mod) is a load error when the trees are built, logged once per server run (`MsmCommands.lastRegistrationErrors()`); the vanilla command stays.
- Creative tabs (ADR 0096 D2): `loader/CreativeTabParser` (closed `Tab`, `Order`, `titleKey` `itemGroup.<ns>.<path>`); `registry/MsmCreativeTabs` registers each tab with `FabricCreativeModeTab.builder()` before the registrar, the icon looked up when drawn (an unknown icon warns after start and shows nothing, as the eject); members come from the registrar's existing `addToTab`; `by_name` sorts the display and search stacks by hover name in a later event phase (stable, as the eject).
- Dev mode: `command` joins `EventOverlay.KINDS_WITH_EVENTS` (its events swap like a key bind's), `creative_tab` joins `KINDS_WITHOUT_EVENTS`.
- `ConformanceCorpusTest` decodes `command-` and `creative-tab-` (PENDING is empty). JUnit `CommandParserTest` 10, `CreativeTabParserTest` 3 (1036 in all). GameTests `MsmCommandGameTest` 13 (plus one manual-only real `/reload`) and `MsmCreativeTabGameTest` 5: 639 per variant on 26.3, 26.4 and `-PwithoutGeckolib`; logs `registered 8 command(s)` and `registered 3 creative tab(s)`.

**Decisions**
- Macro text stays raw (no escaping of `"` or `\`), so the runtime and the eject behave the same; `commands.raw-text` stays.
- Measured macro text: integer `5`, number `2.5`, boolean `1` (a byte), position `1.5 64.0 -2.25`, block position `3 70 -4`. A UUID is no `player` value (vanilla refuses a UUID selector for players); `entity` takes one. `execute as` over two entities gives each function call its own values (the queued function runs before the next fork writes the storage).
- A command with both `function` and `event` runs both, function first (the corpus has it as valid; the validator reports it). The arguments are read even without a function, for the script event, so a selector that matches nobody fails the command (the eject reads them only with a function).
- `as_listed` is registration order: block items, then items, then spawn eggs, each by mod id and file path (scan order), measured in `asListedKeepsTheRegistrationOrder`. This is the eject's order when the project lists its elements by id.
- A real `/reload` would reset the scripts of the tests running alongside, so re-registration is tested on a freshly built `Commands` (which fires the callback as a reload does); the real reload test is manual-only.
- Test items name themselves with `minecraft:custom_name` (`minecraft:item_name` from `msm:components` is overwritten by the item's own name), so `by_name` needs no language on the server. The test monster `monster_spawn`'s egg moved to `msm_test:tab_listed`; the spike test's load-error list names the B454 broken definitions.

**Next**
- B455: fill `CommandEvents.fire` (arguments JSON: numbers, strings and booleans; `players` an array of names; positions arrays of three numbers); `run_script` actions in command events reach `ScriptHost.runAction` with the command id as owner.
- B464: parity of macro values, the fork case and tab order against the eject; `engine-mod/CLAUDE.md` should list `commands/`, the two parsers and `MsmCreativeTabs` at the next status pass.

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B455 Mixins and Script API 1.6

**What**
- The runtime's first two Mixins (ADR 0096 D3), `engine-mod/src/main/java/dev/mcsupermods/runtime/mixin/`, both in `msm_runtime.mixins.json` (common side, `required`, `JAVA_25`), each with its DESIGN section 10 justification comment: `BlockItemPlaceMixin` at the head of `BlockItem.place(BlockPlaceContext)` calls `ScriptBridges.placing` (server only, `ServerPlayer` only, only when `BlockPlaceContext.canPlace()`); a cancel returns `FAIL`, resyncs the inventory, the placement position and its six neighbours, and refuses the rest of a main-hand click (`mainHandCancelled`). `ServerExplosionMixin` at the head of `ServerExplosion.explode()` calls `ScriptBridges.exploding` (`EXPLODE`, `CANCEL` returns 0, `KEEP_BLOCKS` sets a `@Unique` flag that cancels the heads of `interactWithBlocks` and `createFire`).
- Script API 1.6 (ADR 0096 D4, ADR 0095 D5) in `script-api-v1.json`, the typings golden and `scripting/`, every new type, member and event "Since runtime 1.5.1.": `Entity.ride(vehicle)` and `Entity.dismount()` (booleans); `World.itemsNear(pos, radius)` returning the new type `DroppedItem` (`item`, `pos`, `age`, `owner`, `remove()`, `setItem(item)`; `DroppedItemHandle` follows a dimension change); `ItemRef.contents` (`minecraft:container` then `minecraft:bundle_contents`, empty slots left out); events `block.place` (`BlockPlaceEvent`: `pos`, `block`, `item`, `player`, `cancel`), `world.explosion` (`ExplosionEvent`: `pos`, `radius`, `source`, `cause`, `cancel`, `keepBlocks`) and `command` (`CommandEvent`: `id`, `name`, `source`, `args`; not cancellable). `CommandEvents.fire(Identifier id, String name, CommandSourceStack source, JsonObject args)` replaces B454's placeholder (one call line in `MsmCommands.run` changed).
- Plugin tests: snapshot `test/fixtures/previous/script-api-v1-1.9.0.json` (the 1.5 description); `script-api-1-5.test.ts` now pins 1.5 against it; new `script-api-1-6.test.ts`; `typings.test.ts` and `script-api-1-1.test.ts` count the three new events. Scripting plugin 153 tests.
- GameTests: `MsmMixinEventGameTest` 8 (placement fires with position, block, item and count; a cancelled door placement leaves nothing, keeps the stack and resyncs inventory plus seven positions; a dispenser-style placement is not seen; `cancel` stops primed TNT and an ignited creeper; `keepBlocks` keeps all 92 dirt blocks while the pig is hurt; `cancel` wins over `keepBlocks`; a sourceless explosion has cause `block`), `MsmScriptApi16GameTest` 8 (ride and dismount with `vehicle` and `passengers` on a zombie and a pig; the ride reaches the game; riding while riding switches mounts; nothing rides a player; `itemsNear` with `setItem` (capped at 64) and `remove`, owner of a thrown item; `contents` of a bag and a bundle; the `command` event's arguments; an alias from the console and an optional argument). Test script `msm/msm_test/script/api16.js`; `MsmScriptGameTest` counts 26 scripts. `./gradlew build` on 26.3, `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib`: 663 GameTests each, JUnit 1036 (`ScriptApiContractTest` green); client GameTests pass on both versions (26.4 needed a second run: `MsmVehicleClientGameTest` once measured the third-person camera at 6.096 blocks for 6).
- Production jar: the sample mod's content jar with the real runtime jar passed `tools/run-fabric-server` on 26.3 and 26.4 with `--forbid-line 'Mixin apply' --forbid-line 'MixinTransformerError'`; a manual start of the same server with `-Dmixin.debug.verbose=true`, a primed TNT and an ignited creeper logged `Mixing BlockItemPlaceMixin from msm_runtime.mixins.json into net.minecraft.world.item.BlockItem` at start and `Mixing ServerExplosionMixin ... into net.minecraft.world.level.ServerExplosion` at the first explosion, and no Mixin error, on both versions.

**Decisions**
- `Entity.vehicle` and `passengers` of ADR 0096 D4 were already in Script API 1.5 (B421); 1.6 adds only `ride` and `dismount` beside them.
- `ride` gets on unforced (`Entity.startRiding(vehicle)`), so seat limits, mobs that take no riders, sneaking and vanilla's boarding cooldown answer false (measured: a ride right after `dismount` is refused). It refuses riding itself, a loop, another world, removed entities and any player as a mount (vanilla's `/ride` refuses players as mounts; the ADR named players riding players). Riding while riding gets off the first mount (measured).
- `CommandEvent.id` (the definition id) is added beside the ADR's `name` (the primary literal, also for an alias) so a handler can tell commands of two projects apart; `source` is the source entity or undefined (console, command block).
- `world.explosion` fires for every `ServerExplosion` (TNT, creepers, fireballs, wind charges, beds, respawn anchors, `World.explode`, vehicle `explode` actions); `source` is the direct source entity, `cause` its type id or `"block"`. `keepBlocks` also stops the explosion's fire. `block.place` skips placements that cannot happen (`canPlace()` false) but may still fire for one that fails later (an entity in the way).
- Event `source` strings name the Mixins (`BlockItemPlaceMixin`, `ServerExplosionMixin`) and `MsmCommands.run`, as the 1.5 events name runtime listeners.
- `DroppedItem.owner` comes from `ItemEntity.getOwner()`: the thrower while it is loaded, so a player who left reads as none.

**Next**
- B458: the Rules triggers can use `block.place`, `world.explosion` (`cancel`, `keepBlocks`, `cause`) and `command` (`e.id`); "is riding" reads `Entity.vehicle`.
- B462: the sample's Script API 1.6 scripts; one that calls `world.explode` once at `server.started` (with `breaksBlocks: false`) lets a plain server check reach `ServerExplosionMixin`.
- B463: place and explosion triggers in the sim.
- B464: a server check line `--forbid-line 'Mixin apply' --forbid-line 'MixinTransformerError'`; `ServerExplosion` loads only at the first explosion, so the check needs one (above, or a parity GameTest with TNT).
- Limits for B467: a cancelled explosion may still show its smoke and play its bang (the caller sends the explosion packet; not observed in a client); dispensers, endermen and commands placing blocks are not seen; `ride` follows the boarding cooldown.

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B458 Rules: facing, placing, explosions, commands, riding

**What**
- Rules catalogue (ADR 0096 D5): 56 triggers, 44 steps, 19 conditions, 13 values, 7 places (was 51/39/16/12/6).
  - Triggers: `player_mounted` "A player gets on something", `player_dismounted` "A player gets off something", `command_used` "A player types the command" (subject a project `msm:command`), `explosion` "Something explodes" (cancellable), `any_block_placed` "A player places a block" (cancellable; any block or one kind).
  - Steps: `ride` "Ride something" (`mount`: player, mob or other), `dismount` "Get off", `stop_placing` "Stop the placing", `stop_explosion` "Stop the explosion", `keep_blocks_safe` "Keep the blocks safe".
  - Conditions: `is_riding` (`who`, optional `mount` entity type), `is_facing` (`of` here, player, mob or other; `direction` north to down), `caused_by` (`cause` an entity type or `"block"`).
  - Value `facing` "The way it faces" (words, text slots only); place `in_front_of_here` "In front of here".
- Compilation: `command_used` puts plain rules into the command's own `event` (self and other the source), and rules that are not plain go through `run_script` in that event, so the command always has its event; a command with a `function` (which cannot also run an event) sends every rule to a listener of the Script API 1.6 `command` event filtered by `e.id`. `explosion` listens to `world.explosion` (other is `e.source`), `any_block_placed` to `block.place`. Getting on and off has no Script API event: the script looks at each player's `vehicle` every 5 ticks (`rideChange`). Facing reads a block's `facing` property, else its `axis` (x east, y up, z south), and an entity's horizontal direction from `look`.
- New codes `rules.not-for-trigger` (a limited step or condition on another trigger) and `rules.not-a-number` (`facing` in a number slot), with plain words; `RULES_PROBLEM_CODES` 25. New catalogue fields: `StepEntry.triggers`, `ConditionEntry.triggers`, `ValueEntry.words`, `TriggerComponent.bridge` and `unusableWith`, slot and subject type `command`.
- `rules.mcdoc` (493 types; `--check` green), the AI prompt id lists and two prompt sentences, `RulesSection` `THING_WORDS` `msm:command`, the Command Studio test (the Rules section now shows). Commands are named `/name` in the generated scripts' comments.
- Tests: rules plugin 365 (goldens for every new card plus `listener-command_used`, `-explosion`, `-conveyor`; seven compile cases), schemas rules 157, ai 94, app Rules and AI 283; lint and typecheck clean.

**Decisions**
- The brief's mount triggers and `ride`/`dismount` steps go beyond ADR 0096 D5 (which lists the stops and "is riding"); they use only Script API 1.6 members, and the triggers poll because there is no mount event. Mobs getting on things have no trigger (a player trigger's "other" is what was ridden, so `mob_is` on other filters it).
- `caused_by` comes from ADR 0096 D3's Rules wording. `stop_normal_action` also works on the two new cancellable triggers.
- No command argument value: the ADR lists none; rules cannot read what was typed yet.
- No new Rules templates (pinned by the library and exporters tests; B461).

**Next**
- App (B424a or later): pickers for the `command` slot and subject sort (`SUBJECT_SORTS`), a `mount` picker without "every player", `facing` offered only in text slots, the `of` and `direction` choices.

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B469 spike: traders, professions, mount storage and shoulders

What
- Answered S11–S13 of `docs/PLAN-vanilla-parity-2.md` by observation on 26.3 and 26.4-snapshot-7: throwaway GameTests (5, GameTest server) and one client GameTest on a dedicated server (`createServer()`/`connect()`, headless Mesa EGL) over a runtime `mob` body implementing `Merchant`, a rideable `animal` body implementing `HasCustomInventoryScreen`, a small tamed `animal` body on the player's shoulder (as a passenger and as a perched follower), two job site blocks with POI types (one in `#minecraft:acquirable_job_site`, one not), two professions with project trade sets and red/blue profession textures. Spike code deleted afterwards; `./gradlew build` green on both versions. Results, logs, screenshots and a copy of the spike source are in the scratchpad (`b469/`); the findings are in the B469 report for the plan's "Notes from implementation".

Decisions
- S11: `VillagerTrade.getOffer` needs `LootContextParamSets.VILLAGER_TRADE` with ORIGIN, THIS_ENTITY and ADDITIONAL_COST_COMPONENT_ALLOWED (all required; each left out throws), random from the trade set's `random_sequence`. A `PathfinderMob` implementing `Merchant` opens vanilla's merchant screen from a real right click, with offers, the XP bar, the level name and out-of-stock crosses; level-ups and restocks reach the open screen through `sendMerchantOffers`. Vanilla trades with a `merchant_predicate` on `minecraft:villager/variant` return null for a non-villager (armourer level 5 gives a project mob no offers at all).
- S12, go for ADR 0098 D2 on both versions: Fabric `PoiHelper` on 26.3, reflection into the private `PoiTypes.register(ResourceKey, Set, int, int)` on 26.4 (no Mixin, reserve B487 not needed). A vanilla villager takes the job only when the POI is in `#minecraft:acquirable_job_site`. Textures: `<ns>:textures/entity/villager/profession/<path>.png` and `zombie_villager/profession/`. Registering a POI on a state that already has one throws only after it has replaced the vanilla mapping, so the runtime must check `PoiTypes.hasPoi` for every state first.
- S13: the inventory key opens `openCustomInventoryScreen` for any ridden mob implementing `HasCustomInventoryScreen`, on both versions. `Entity.startRiding` refuses a player as vehicle on the server (`EntityType.canSerialize`), even forced; go for D4 as a perched follower (synched flag, position from the owner every tick on both sides), not a passenger.

Next
- The main session copies the report's notes into the plan and ADR 0098 (D4 mechanism change); Wave 10 (B472, B473) may start.
## 2026-11-15 — executor — B470 spike: fluids in the real game

What
- Answered S14 of `docs/PLAN-vanilla-parity-2.md` (ADR 0099 D3) by observation on 26.3 and 26.4-snapshot-7: throwaway GameTests (30, on the GameTest server, in a 23 by 23 walled pool structure) and one client GameTest (singleplayer, then `createServer()`/`connect()` on a dedicated server, headless Mesa EGL) over five directly registered test fluids with their `LiquidBlock` and `BucketItem`: a water-like and a lava-like fluid that apply their own entity effects, the same two without effects (tag only), and a fluid in no tag; vanilla water and lava as controls. Measured flow, falling, draining, infinite sources, bucket fill and empty (mock player and the use key on the dedicated server), dispensers, drawing through `FluidRenderingRegistry` (screenshots and `assertScreenshotContains` for the tint), swimming, drowning, putting out fire, lava burning, fall damage, fog and mixing. A spike Mixin on `Entity.isInWater`/`isInLava` was tried on 26.4. Spike code deleted afterwards; `./gradlew build` green on both versions (663 GameTests each). Results, screenshots, logs and a copy of the spike source are in the scratchpad (`b470/`), the findings in the B470 report for the plan's "Notes from implementation".

Decisions
- Go for 26.3: vanilla's `FlowingFluid` (source and flowing classes), `LiquidBlock`, `BucketItem` and `FluidRenderingRegistry` do everything with our numbers; `#minecraft:water` gives swimming, drowning, buoyancy, fog and no fall damage; putting out fire and lava burning come from the fluid's own `entityInside` (`InsideBlockEffectType.EXTINGUISH`, `LAVA_IGNITE` and `lavaHurt`), not from the tag.
- Go for 26.4 only with one Mixin (a head injection into `Entity.isInWater` and `isInLava` answering from the fluid tag height): without it a project fluid in `#minecraft:water` drowns entities but is never "in water", so players move as in lava, items sink and nothing floats. Fog on 26.4 comes from `Fluid.Properties.fogType`, the swimming pose from `#minecraft:swimmable`. If the Mixin is refused, 26.4 is a no-go and reserve B486 applies.
- Mixing is not absent as ADR 0099 D5 says: on 26.3 a lava-like fluid in `#minecraft:lava` makes obsidian and cobblestone with any water by vanilla's rule; on 26.4 only vanilla lava does.

Next
- Main session: record the S14 answers in "Notes from implementation" and ADR 0099's findings, decide the 26.4 Mixin (an ADR 0099 amendment), then B472 and B473.

## 2026-11-15 — executor — B468a Turn into rules events, compressed PNGs

What
- "Turn into rules" (`app/src/renderer/src/studios/rules/turn-into-rules.ts`): `eventAt` now reads the hand-made event with the rules compiler's own `handMadeEvents` (exported by `@msm/plugin-rules`), so it finds events in a list field (a vehicle's `weapons[].on_fire`) and in a top-level `{ event }` object (a vehicle's `on_tick`) as well as the component and plain-field forms. `releaseTrigger` takes the reference away in those two forms too: the field of every list entry, or the object's `event` with its option fields moved onto the rule (`on_tick.interval` 40 becomes `interval_seconds: 2`), the object removed when left empty. The option move is shared with the component case (`takeOptions`). Two new tests in `app/test/turn-into-rules.test.ts`.
- `encodePng` (`packages/plugins/library/src/assets/png.ts`) writes one fixed-Huffman deflate block with greedy LZ77 matches (hash chains, 32 KiB window, 128 tries) instead of stored blocks, with the same zlib header (`78 01`) and Adler-32. No dependency; integer maths only, so the bytes are stable. A flat 16x16 picture is 78 bytes (was 1108); the 70 placeholder patterns total 11,403 bytes (was 111,690); the 64x64 skin 284 (was 16,516). The 598 PNGs in `examples/`, `fixtures/sample-*` and the library's test fixtures went from 2,461,737 to 121,542 bytes.
- Goldens regenerated with `UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` (library and exporters): only `.png` files and the content-jar and Java-eject SHA-256 pins (`packages/exporters/test/fixtures/mc-26.*/*.sha256`, which hash archives holding those PNGs) changed. The pinned pattern and skin hashes in `png.test.ts` were updated. New round-trip tests (flat, noisy, a picture over the 32 KiB window, every pattern size) decode through Node's `inflateSync`.
- Tests that leaned on stored blocks: `art.test.ts` checked a length over 1000 bytes (now checks the inflated rows against `generateArt`); `app/test/components/wizard-image.test.tsx` needed a PNG over 4 KB (now a noisy one); `sample-vehicles.golden.test.ts`'s `compactPng` (fflate level 9) is now as small as the library's output for one picture, so its check is "no larger" and its comment says why it stays (the fixture's bytes).

Decisions
- A list trigger is offered only when every entry names the same event: the rules compiler writes the generated event into every entry, so a hand-made event on some weapons only would not round-trip.
- Fixed Huffman codes rather than dynamic ones: small, enough for placeholder pictures, and no new dependency (fflate stays a dev dependency of `@msm/exporters` only). Filter type stays none, as the in-repo PNG readers (`pixelsOf` in the exporters tests, the library tests) expect.

Next
- Main session: review and merge `b468a`. Turbo caches `test` per package without its workspace dependencies (`dependsOn: []`), so a library change replays the exporters' cached run; run `turbo run test --force` (or the exporters package directly) after library asset changes.

## 2026-11-21 — executor — B490 updates install on close; plugin API Java project input

**What**
- Updates install when the app closes (the user's answer of 2026-11-21): `app/src/main/updater.ts` sets `autoInstallOnAppQuit` on, so electron-updater's quit handler runs the downloaded installer silently (`--updated /S`, the app is not started again) when the app quits with exit code 0. Restart to update is unchanged (`quitAndInstall(true, true)`, installs once; electron-updater's own quit skips the quit handler). The close guard still runs first: the app quits only after every window has closed, so Cancel or a failed save installs nothing, and a close after Save or Discard installs. The rules on what is offered (no pre-releases or downgrades, no web installer, only packaged on Windows outside test runs) are unchanged.
- Wording: the banner reads "Version X is ready and installs when you close MCSuperMods —" with Restart to update; the Check for Updates toast and the Windows notification say the same; the guide's updates paragraph (`docs/guide/getting-started.md`), DESIGN Open Question 4, ADR 0018 (amendment of 2026-11-21) and CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` "Changed".
- Tests: `app/test/main-updater-feed.test.ts` gains six cases with electron-updater's real `NsisUpdater` behind MSM's close guard and main's `window-all-closed` step (clean close, Save, Discard, Cancel and a failed save, a non-zero exit code, Restart to update installing once); `main-updater.test.ts` and the banner tests follow the new option and wording.
- Plugin API 1.18.0 (unreleased, no bump) declares `JavaProjectInput.commands?` and `creativeTabs?` (`DefinitionInput[]`, ADR 0096 D6); the exporter passes them as ordinary fields, and the 26.3 generator's `GeneratorInput` workaround is gone (it uses `JavaProjectInput`). Type and routing tests added in `packages/plugin-api/test/types.test.ts` and `packages/exporters/test/java-project.test.ts`; ADR 0096's open item is marked resolved.

**Decisions**
- Install on close relies on electron-updater's own `autoInstallOnAppQuit` handler rather than a second MSM path, so the exit-code and "already installing" rules are electron-updater's; it adds the handler when a download finishes, which is why the option is set when the updater loads.

**Next**
- The Windows check in `docs/HANDOFF.md` (updater item (c)) should add: with a downloaded update, close the window (after Save, Discard, or with nothing unsaved): no installer pages show, and the next start runs the new version with What's new once. HANDOFF's open question 3 is answered. README's "Releasing" text still says the update installs when the user chooses Restart to update.
## 2026-11-21 — executor — B488 world backups before installing

**What**
- ADR 0102 D1–D3. Before a data pack goes into `<gameDir>/saves/<world>/datapacks/`, main zips the whole world into `<msmHome>/backups/<location>/<world-dir>/<YYYY-MM-DD_HH-mm-ss>.zip` (`app/src/main/platform/world-backups.ts`, called from `installDataPack` in `minecraft.ts` after the existing containment checks). The zip is streamed with fflate (already a dependency) into a temporary file beside it and renamed into place; the oldest beyond `backups.keep` are deleted only after a new backup succeeded; a failed backup stops the install with "The world could not be backed up, so nothing was installed: <reason> …". The location folder is `<launcher>-<instance|default>-<8 hex of the root's SHA-1>`.
- Settings `backups.beforeInstall` (default on) and `backups.keep` (default 5, 1 to 50), stored only when not the defaults; zod-validated in `settings:get|set`. `installDataPack` answers `{ path, backup }`. New channels `msm:v1:worldBackups:list|restore|openFolder` (`PlatformAdapter.worldBackups`, optional like `tryItWorlds`).
- Restore unpacks a backup into the same `saves/` as `<world-dir>-restored-<stamp>` (`-2`, `-3` when taken), through a temporary folder renamed into place; entry names are checked segment by segment, so a planted zip cannot write outside the new folder.
- Renderer: `components/WorldBackupsSection.tsx` in Settings ("World backups": the folder with Open folder, "Back up a world before installing into it", "Backups to keep per world", the backups per world with Restore); the install message adds "The world was backed up first as <file> (Settings, World backups)." through `session/install-backups.ts`, which wraps the platform handed to the session in `main.tsx` (`project-session.ts` is untouched; it drops the backup field).
- Tests: `test/main-world-backups.test.ts` (10), `test/components/settings-world-backups.test.tsx` (5), settings and IPC contract samples, the App install message; e2e `datapack-path` checks the zip, the message, the Settings list and a Restore. Guide: `playing-and-testing.md#world-backups`, a line in `getting-started.md`.

**Decisions**
- `session.lock` is left out of the zip (Minecraft's own Make Backup does the same; the game may hold it locked), and symbolic links inside a world are neither followed nor copied. Already-compressed files (`.mca`, `.dat`, `.png` and similar) are stored, the rest deflated.
- fflate writes no ZIP64, so a world over 4 GB or 65,535 files fails its backup with a clear reason (and the install stops); the setting turns backups off for such worlds.
- Entries sit under `<world-dir>/` like the game's own backup zips, so a zip can also be unzipped into `saves` by hand.

**Next**
- In-game check on Windows: install into a real world with Minecraft closed, restore, open the restored copy.
- `app/CLAUDE.md` contents line for `world-backups.ts`, `WorldBackupsSection.tsx` and the `worldBackups:*` channels (not in this brief's files).

## 2026-11-21 — executor — the shoulder pet sneak GameTest

**What**
- Root cause of the flaky `aPerchedPetStaysOnTheShoulderThroughATeleportAndIsSaved` ("sneaking kept the pet on on tick 8", CI run 44948669629 on 8fdd516, both versions): the test teleported the owner 7 blocks east and 3 south (`owner.position().add(7, 0, 3)`), which can carry the perched pet out of the test's 8 by 8 box. The GameTest server force-loads only the chunks that box touches (`TestInstanceBlockEntity.forceLoadChunks`), its simulation distance is 0, and a mock player's simulation ticket stays at the chunk it joined in (`ServerPlayer.teleportTo` does not call `ServerChunkCache.move`; only a client's position packet does). Test positions are random per run, so whenever a chunk border fell between the box's edge and the destination, the pet was in a chunk that is not entity-ticking: it stopped ticking, `MobShoulder.tick` never ran and the sneak was never seen. Reproduced with temporary prints: the failing run had the pet one block past the box (`forced=false`, `petTicking=false`) and its tick count did not move in the two ticks after the sneak; a passing run had `forced=true` and two pet ticks.
- Fix (test only, `engine-mod/src/gametest/java/dev/mcsupermods/runtime/gametest/MsmMobStorageGameTest.java`): the teleport goes to (6.5, 2, 6.5) in the test's own box (still about 6.4 blocks from the start), with an assertion that the pet's place on the shoulder stays inside `helper.getBounds()`, and a comment saying why.
- The runtime was not at fault: once the pet ticks, sneaking takes it off on its next tick. In a real game the player's own ticket follows the player and keeps the pet's chunk ticking. The other tests in the class keep the pet inside the box (the dimension change moves only the owner), so they do not have this fragility.

**Decisions**
- No longer delays and no `succeedWhen`: the unperch is deterministic once the pet ticks, so the fixed two ticks stay.

**Next**
- Any future GameTest that moves a mock player and expects nearby mobs to keep ticking must stay inside its test box (or call `ServerChunkCache.move` for the player, which still covers only its own chunk at simulation distance 0).

## 2026-11-21 — executor — B400 Try it script worker and Script API shim

**What**
- `packages/sim/src/script/` (ADR 0085 D9 slice 4): `shim.ts` `createScriptRuntime(init, modules)` builds every object a script sees from `script-api-v1.json`; each declared member (types with their `extends`, `msm` namespaces, `require`) is either implemented or a stub that says "<Type.member>, used by the script <id>" once as Only in Minecraft and returns a neutral value of its declared type (a stub object for a declared type, the first literal of a union). Implemented: `msm.version`, `log`, `events.on` (with `player.tick` `interval`), `actions.define`, `schedule` (on the area clock), `storage` and `Entity.data` (in memory, kept across reloads and restarts), `players`, `getWorld` (this world only), `require` (CommonJS, relative ids in the namespace, `msm:runtime`, once each), `Pos`, `World.dimension/time/getBlock/setBlock/spawnParticle/playSound/entitiesNear`, entity identity (`type`, `uuid`, `pos`, `world`, `name`, `isPlayer`, `isAlive`, `asPlayer`), `Player.isSneaking/heldItem/give/hasItem/sendMessage`, `BlockRef`, `ItemRef.id/count`, event members the bridge sends, `cancel()`, `keepBlocks()`. The function is self-contained, so it is serialised into the worker.
- `bridge.ts` `ScriptBridge`: one message at a time with the blocks changed since the last (the whole area after a ground load or above 4,096 changes), applies set blocks (catalogue, neighbour updates), particles, sounds, messages (a "What happened" line and a player chip, not the chat box), items given (the area's inventory) and store writes, in the order the script did them; `ask` holds a cancellable click until the answer; a time-out is reported and the scripts start again. `runner.ts` (`ScriptRunner`, `inProcessRunner`), `protocol.ts`, `sources.ts` (`scriptSources`), `api.ts` (`apiMembers`).
- Wiring (`local-source.ts`, `LocalSourceOptions.scripts`, `loadScripts`): `block.interact` first on a right click on a block, `block.break` before breaking, `block.place` before a held block is placed, `entity.interact`, `item.use` (bags in the air), `world.explosion` (the Explode tool) wait for the answer; `entity.death` after a hit, `command` and `player.chat` from the chat box, `server.tick`, `player.tick`, and `server.started` then `player.join` after the first load. `run_script` calls the defined handler (`ActionHost.scripts`; rule bridges say "Rule "<name>" ran as a script."). Events the preview never fires (hurt, damaged, respawn, leave, dimension change, keys, vehicles) are said once per script. `TriggerEngine` no longer says scripts run only in the game when they run; `CommandHost.listeners` gets the name and arguments, `said` the plain chat lines; `Types2Area` takes `commandUsed`, `chatSaid` and `explode(pos, decided)`.
- B463 agreement: with the scripts running, the place, explosion and command decisions are the scripts' own answer and the script text is not read (prefer the worker); without them (every B463 test) nothing changed. `test/script/vanilla-blocks.test.ts` shows both agree on the fixture (cobweb stopped, the Explode tool breaks), and that the worker also runs the hand-written `block.place` listener the text reading can only name (bedrock).
- App: `tryit/script-worker.ts` `createWorkerRunner` (a classic `blob:` worker built from the wrapped scripts, `createScriptRuntime.toString()` and `scriptWorkerMain`, which removes network, storage, worker and timer globals and `postMessage` before any script runs; answers on the next task so Promise callbacks are in; `SCRIPT_BUDGET_MS` 2,000 per call, then the worker is terminated and the call answers `timedOut`). `session-source.ts` `TryItArea` option `scripts` (`transpile`, `api`, `runner`): the lowered scripts are transpiled by the session's scripting service in main and loaded whenever their sources change. `TryItView` passes `window.msm.scripting` and `SCRIPT_API` (prop `scripting`, `null` turns scripts off).
- Tests: sim `test/script/` (api walk 5, sample-script 8, shim 8, bridge 2, vanilla blocks 5; 580 sim tests), app `test/components/tryit/script-worker.test.ts` (6: the worker script run in a `node:vm` context, stripped globals, Promise callbacks, the budget, an area loading scripts, an endless loop in "What happened"; 2466 app tests), e2e `tryit-path` gains "the sample script runs in the script worker, and an endless loop is stopped" (6 of 6 green; `fluid-path` and `trader-path` green).
- Sizes: `TryItView` 344.0 kB (was 315.7 kB), renderer 16.2 MB of 18 (+28.6 kB in all), `app.asar` 29.1 MB of 32. Importing the scripting plugin into the Try it chunk folds the lazy `turn-into-rules` chunk (158 kB) into `index` (+63 kB) and `src`; the total grows only by the Try it code.

**Decisions**
- CSP: no change and no `'unsafe-eval'`. The production policy (`script-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self'`) allows the worker as built, the same way as the plugin sandbox: nothing is evaluated from text, the scripts are part of the worker's own `blob:` script. Checked in the packaged renderer under `msm-app://` by the e2e step.
- The shim runs inside the worker on a copy of the area, so scripts get answers at once (`getBlock` after `setBlock` sees the change); the bridge applies what they did when the answer comes. Effects of a `run_script` handler and of non-cancellable events show after the event's other actions (a few milliseconds later), an approximation the guide should name.
- The player is named `Player` (the chat box's `PREVIEW_PLAYER_NAME`); `msm.version` is `try-it` unless the host passes one (the view passes none).
- Script messages go to "What happened" and a chip, not the chat box, so `/greet`'s own answer stays the last chat line.

**Next**
- B401: name each rule's step and error from the `// rule:<key>` markers (the bridge already gives rule-book origins for generated scripts and runs their handlers).
- Fire `key.pressed`/`key.released` and the `vehicle.*` events from `controls/` and `vehicles/` (said once as not fired yet).
- B402 guide rows: scripts now run in Try it (members that need the game are said), the 2-second stop, effects a moment after the event's other actions, messages in "What happened".

## 2026-11-21 — executor — B401 logic Rules in Try it's log

**What**
- `packages/sim/src/script/rule-steps.ts` (new): `instrumentRuleScript(source)` rewrites a generated Rules script (ADR 0082 D3) in place at its `// rule:<key>` lines, in the compiler's own shapes only, keeping every line (transpile problems keep their line numbers): `rule(key, ...)` becomes `__tryIt.rule`, the rule's `only if` and `if` steps go through `__tryIt.check`, `Math.random() * 100 < P` through `__tryIt.chance(P)`, `repeat` (plain and with a wait) through `__tryIt.repeat`, `for each player` through `__tryIt.each`, the alive check after a wait through `__tryIt.gone`; the hooks are imported from `msm:try-it` on the `msm:runtime` import line. Shapes not recognised are left as they are. `scriptSources` instruments the scripts that carry the "Made by Rules from" line, so the app's transpile and the tests both get it.
- Shim (`shim.ts`): the `msm:try-it` module; while a rule runs, every op and line carries its key (`ScriptStep.rule`), and its `msm.schedule` callbacks run with the key again (a wait on the area's clock). New `rule` lines (`RuleStep`: `start` from a Script API event, `check`, `chance`, `repeat`, `each`, `wait`, `resume`, `gone`, `error` with the step it was in). An error stops only that rule, as the script's own helper does. Chances follow the area's "Run every time" (`WorldSync.chance`), seeded otherwise (`ScriptRuntimeInit.seed`). "Only in Minecraft" members are said once per script, member and rule.
- Bridge (`bridge.ts`): lines of a rule are named `Rule "<name>"` (the book's name through the new `ScriptBridgeHost.ruleName`, else the key) with `ruleKey`/`ruleBook` in the origin, so they link to the rule card; counters (`rules.counter.<name>`) are said; a tick rule whose "only if" is false is said once, not every tick; the generated script's own error line ("Rules <book>, rule <key>: ...") is named by the rule too. `TraceEntry.ruleStep` (`trace.ts`) records the step (`did` for what the rule did).
- `local-source.ts` (two lines): passes `ruleName` and `chance` to the bridge, and keeps `options.ruleBooks` for naming (before, only `setRuleBooks` set them, so B463's world events and the bridge could not name rules given at construction).
- App: `WhatHappenedEntry.ruleStep` (`session-source.ts`, one field); `WhatHappened.tsx` puts a rule's step lines one step further in (`lineClass`) and gives them `data-rule-step`.
- Tests: sim `test/script/rule-steps.test.ts` (21: every compiler golden instrumented, same line count, transpiles; `fixtures/sample-rules` "Try your luck", "Rally the players nearby" (wait of 40 ticks on the clock), the world rules; the library's "Open a lucky block", "Spend a lucky coin", "Watch the players nearby"; the six rules templates compiled by the rules plugin; the `step-repeat` golden with waits; seeded chances; errors named by the rule and step, with and without instrumentation); `vanilla-blocks.test.ts` updated (the generated script's messages are now named by the rule). 601 sim tests. App: `WhatHappened.test.tsx` (+1), `script-worker.test.ts` (+1, a generated script through the worker); 2468 app tests. e2e `tryit-path` gains "a logic rule says its steps by the rule, from the script worker (B401)" (7 of 7 green; one earlier full run had the B463 bag-screen test time out once under load, green alone and on the rerun); `rules-path` green. `TryItView` 351.3 kB (was 344.0), renderer 16.2 MB of 18.

**Decisions**
- Step names come from what a step is and does, not from step numbers: the compiler moves the steps after a wait into nested functions, so the order in the script is not the order on the card. An error says the last step it reached ("failed after its "if" check", "in time 2 of its repeat", "after its wait of 2 seconds").
- A rule run by `run_script` has no start line of its own (the action already says "Rule "<name>" ran as a script."); a rule started by a Script API event says "The script heard <event>, so rule "<name>" ran." as a trigger line.

Every other block keeps its one-colour cube; water, lava and bubble columns stay plain, as before.
- `app/src/renderer/src/tryit/render/fallback-colours.ts`: `DRAWN_RECIPES`, `FallbackLook.drawn` (the recipe of each face), texture ids `msm:tryit_drawn/<recipe>/<rrggbb>/<block path>` (`drawnTextureId`, `parseDrawnTextureId`) and `fallbackTexturePng(id)` (async: a drawn face through `artLookPng`, or the plain picture). The library is imported on the first drawn face with a dynamic `import('@msm/plugin-library')` (only a type import at the top), so the lazy canvas chunk loads as quickly as before: a static import made the two happy-dom "no WebGL" boundary tests time out while the chunk loaded. The library is already in the main chunk, so this downloads nothing.
- Wiring in `resources.ts` (two lines): the texture step calls `await fallbackTexturePng(id)` in place of `parseFallbackTextureId` and `fallbackPicture`. `resources.test.ts`: the grass and stone assertion counts `msm:tryit_drawn/` textures (still 4).
- Tests: `fallback-colours.test.ts` 6 (was 3): the families and their recipes per face, colours from the table, per-block seeds, every recipe drawn by the library (no stub) and a block face, other blocks and liquids still one colour, drawn bytes equal the library's, 16 by 16, leaves with clear pixels. App 2471 tests green; `tryit-path` 7 of 7 under `xvfb-run -a` after `pnpm build`; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, check-deps pass. Renderer 16.3 MB of 18; `TryItView` 351.3 kB, unchanged.
- Frame rate, Island seed 1234, canvas 640 by 360, Smaller picture off, SwiftShader, three runs of 8 seconds each, same session, built alternately with and without the change: the machine's load was 10 to 33 (other workers), so the numbers move with the load more than with the build. Before (load 19 to 33): 12 to 28 fps, median about 17. After (load 20 to 30): 13 to 26, median about 17; at load 10 to 14: 23 to 38. Geometry, atlas pass and draw calls are unchanged (only the pixels of about 30 atlas pictures differ), so no difference was expected and none was seen; B405's 22 to 23 fps was not reproducible at this load either way.

**Decisions**
- Seeds are per block id, so stone and andesite of the same recipe differ and each block id always gives the same bytes; one picture per block face, shared by every block of that id.

## 2026-11-21 — executor — app tests reliable under load

**What**
- Lazy chunks (`key-bind-studio`, `hud-studio`, `vehicle-studio`, `TryItScene`, `RulesSection`): each Studio, the Rules section and Try it's canvas are `React.lazy` imports, which Vitest transforms on first use; under load that took longer than `findBy`'s one-second default ("Loading the Key bind Studio…", "Unable to find vehicle-studio", no alert from the canvas, and `RulesSection`'s "is in the Block, Item, Mob and Effect Studios" in a whole-monorepo `turbo run test`). Reproduced with eight busy loops alongside. New `app/test/components/lazy-chunks.ts`: the files load the lazy modules in `beforeAll` (`preloadChunks`, the component's own `import()` then resolves from the module cache; 60 s hook budget) and wait for what they render with `LAZY_CHUNK_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s); the controls harness's `openStudio` uses it for both controls Studios.
- `RulesSection` "flushing held-back typing resolves once the edit is in the project": the host's `applyChanges` waited a real 30 ms and the test checked after a real 5 ms, then after React's `act`, which can run past the 30 ms under load. The host now waits on a gate the test opens (`applyGate`), so the check that the flush has not settled before the edit lands no longer depends on the clock. Still fails when the section's flush does not return its edit chain (checked by breaking it).
- `App.test.tsx` "notes on a vanilla pack export": the same cause as the world picker test fixed earlier today. Its function matcher (`content.includes(MSM_CONTENT_NOTE)`) also matches Radix Toast's screen-reader copy (probed: two elements 200 ms after the toast), which stays one second, as long as `findBy` waits; when the first query came after that copy appeared, the query could fail. It now goes through the file's `toast` helper (which ignores `body > [role="status"]`; its type is now `Matcher`). The other App queries match only the visible toast or dialogs.
- e2e `tryit-path` bag screen (B463): reproduced unloaded on the second of two runs (the satchel said "opens only while you sneak" on the sneaking use). A real bug in `@msm/sim`: a use that waits for the scripts' answer (`item.use`, `block.interact`, `entity.interact`, `block.place`) read the player's sneaking when the answer came, and the test (like a quick player) had let go of Shift by then. `PlayerController.asOfUse` and `LocalWorldSource.asOfNow` now decide those uses with the sneaking of the moment they were made, as the game does in that tick; sim test `bridge.test.ts` "decides a use with the sneaking of the moment it was made" (fails before the fix). The spec's `sneakUse` also waits for ticks after Shift goes down (the readout's `data-tick`, two refreshes) instead of a fixed 300 ms.
- Runs: the five component files `--repeats 30` under eight busy loops, and three cold runs of them under load, green; App's two toast tests `--repeats 30` under load green; `turbo run test --force --filter=@msm/app --filter=@msm/exporters` three times in a row green (2468 app tests each), and once more with `@msm/sim` (602); `tryit-path` twice under `xvfb-run -a` after `pnpm build` (7 of 7 each) and its bag test `--repeat-each 5` under six busy loops; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`.

**Decisions**
- Lazy chunks are preloaded rather than every `findBy` getting a long timeout alone: the test then waits for the module, not for a guess at how long the transform takes; the longer `findBy` timeout stays as a backstop for the first render.
- No retries, no skipped tests, no assertion loosened.

**Next**
- A whole-monorepo `turbo run test` also timed out `packages/sim` `test/script/rule-steps.test.ts` "keeps every line, instruments every rule and still transpiles" at the sim package's default 5 s (it transpiles every compiler golden); outside this brief.
- Other component tests that `findBy` a lazy Studio or section without preloading (`RuleBookStudio`, `rules-project-pickers`, `rules-b458a-pickers`, `command-studio`, `profession-studio`, `fluid-studio`, `creative-tab-studio`, `particle-studio`) can use `lazy-chunks.ts` the same way if they show the same failure.

D3: strip, flatten, till and wax by callback on both versions, burn by the `Flammability` routes; only `age` on 26.4 needs reserve B546.

  - `MsmMultifaceBlock` (`GlowLichenBlock`): `light`, `spreads`, `waterloggable`.
  - `MsmBigDripleafBlock` (`BigDripleafBlock`), `MsmDripleafStemBlock` (`BigDripleafStemBlock`, the `<path>_stem`) and `MsmSmallDripleafBlock` (`SmallDripleafBlock`, a double-high item): own survival, stacking, bone meal and growing into `grows_into`; vanilla's tilt at `[2, 10, 10]`, our own tilt timing otherwise.

- `DefinitionScanner.KINDS` takes `vanilla_block_rules`; `EventOverlay.KINDS_WITHOUT_EVENTS` too (an overlay for it needs a restart). `LoadReport.withProblems`.
- GameTests: `MsmOwnSoundsGameTest` 6 (own place and step sounds heard, a door with `block_sounds` places with its own sound, own door open and close sounds, a door hands cannot open, an iron-based trapdoor that hands open, own button press and release sounds, a plate only mobs press, unknown events and the missing 26.4 entry reported) and `MsmVanillaPairsGameTest` 7 (strip, flatten, till with drops, a rule replacing vanilla's coarse dirt pair, vanilla's own pairs untouched, air above and the bottom face, wax and unwax, project components winning over a file, the warnings, burning smooth basalt against cobblestone, ageing an oxidised copper grate on 26.3), on new `msm_test` blocks `sound_*`, `set_*`, `tools_dirt`, `vp_*`, rules files `vr_a`/`vr_b` and two `block_sound_set` entries. 743 GameTests per variant.

**Decisions**
- The block classes take their set type from the shared `BlockTypes`/`Weathering` code through `BlockSetTypes.of(SetType)`, and neither file is this brief's; so `OwnSounds.soundTypeFor` (called just before each block is built) prepares the block's own set type and `BlockExtras.apply` (right after) clears it, and `of` answers it for that one block. A follow-up can pass the definition instead.
- A block's own component wins over a rules file for the same change (warning); between files the later wins (warning). Rules naming a block not registered at start-up are skipped with a warning; `into` and `drops` are looked up on use and checked once after start-up (`BlockExtras.lateWarnings()`, log only).
- The shield rule stays for the axe only; shovels and hoes ignore the off hand.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — every vanilla sound type in sound_type

**What**
- Bug (CI run 44988128993, both engine-mod jobs): `fixtures/sim-parity` blocks with `sound_type` `big_dripleaf`, `glow_lichen` and `small_dripleaf` passed the app (real vanilla sound types) but the runtime knew only the format's 40 names, skipped the blocks, and their loot tables then failed the whole `sim_parity` data pack, so `runGameTest` failed.
- Format (vanilla parity): `::msm::definition::SoundType` is now `(SoundTypeName | string)`, any vanilla sound type name of the target; the 40 names stay as the enum `SoundTypeName`, which the Block Studio still offers as its choices. `symbols.json` regenerated (541 types). Corpus: `block-bad-sound-type.json` (`squeaky`) is structurally valid now and moved to `valid/block-sound-type-unlisted-name.json`; new `valid/block-sound-type-glow-lichen.json` and `invalid/block-sound-type-number.json` (`schema.no-union-match`).
- Runtime: `loader/MsmSoundType` is a record of the name (constants `STONE`, `GLASS`, `WOOD`), parsed without bootstrap. The `registry/BlockSounds` seam resolves it per version from vanilla's own public static fields: 26.3 every `SoundType` constant by lower-case name (131), 26.4 every `BlockSoundSets` key by path (137) with `amethyst` to `amethyst_block`. An unknown name is a load error that skips the block (`sound_type "x" is not a sound type of this Minecraft version (26.x); the block is skipped`).
- Plugin: `blocks-items.sound-type-unknown` is an error for any name outside the target's `soundTypes` (through `FORMAT_SOUND_SET_ALIASES`), not only names outside the 40; `FORMAT_SOUND_TYPES` documents the editor's suggestions.
- Java eject (26.3): the `sound_type` reader takes every 26.3 name; the list moved from `target.ts` into `packages/targets/mc-26.3/src/sound-types.ts`, shared by the target facts and `java-project/blocks.ts`.
- GameTests (`MsmOwnSoundsGameTest`): `aBlockWithTheGlowLichenSoundTypePlacesWithGlowLichensSound` (block `sound_glow_lichen` registers, has the glow lichen sound type and plays vanilla glow lichen's place sound when a player places it) and `anUnknownSoundTypeIsALoadErrorThatSkipsTheBlock` (`unknown_sound_type.json`, listed in `MsmSpikeGameTest`'s expected errors); the `BlockSoundCheck` seams gain `glow_lichen` and `placeSound`. 759 GameTests per variant, on 26.3, 26.4 and without GeckoLib, the `sim_parity` data pack loading.

**Decisions**
- Parsing accepts any string, as the mcdoc does; whether the version has the name is the registrar's check, so the corpus stays identical on both sides.
- The Block Studio's "Sound type" picker still lists only the 40 suggestions (no app change in this brief); other names work through Raw JSON and the advanced form.

**Next**
- Suggested: the Block Studio's "Sound type" choices from the target's `blocks.soundTypes`, so every vanilla name can be picked.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — two CI flakes: the Profession Studio picture and leaf decay

**What**
- `app/test/components/studios/entities/profession-studio.test.tsx` "copies a picked picture…" (CI run 44992358215): the cause was in `IdInput`, not the test. A field shown by a lazy chunk is committed in one Scheduler task and has its passive effects flushed in a later one; RTL's `findBy` drains with `setTimeout(0)`, which under load can run before that `setImmediate`. The typed text then met the mount effect `setText(value)` at the change event and was reset to `''`, so blur committed nothing (the CI dump showed the villager picture field empty and no error). `app/src/renderer/src/forms/IdInput.tsx` now resets its text when `value` changes during render (the stored-previous-value pattern) instead of in an effect. New `app/test/components/id-input.test.tsx` types in the microtask right after the reveal commit: it fails on the old `IdInput` with the CI's symptom and passes now.
- Parity `sample_mod_block_types_parity_test_leaves_decay_away_from_logs` (CI run 44994558212): the far leaves were placed non-persistent, so once their scheduled tick set `distance=7` (tick 1) any of the level's own random ticks could decay them before the tick-3 check. They now start `persistent=true` (distance is still worked out, as vanilla's leaves do), are checked at `distance=7`, and are set to `persistent=false,distance=7` only just before the test's own `randomTick`. With `random_tick_speed 4096` added for a trial, the old test failed with the CI message and the new one passed (trial line removed).
- Checked: the profession and IdInput tests 30 runs green under 8 busy loops (3 at a time); parity `sample_mod_*` on the content jars, 26.3 five runs and 26.4 three runs, 83 of 83 each; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `@msm/app` tests (2562), `./gradlew -p parity build`. Build outputs deleted.

**Decisions**
- Fixed the component rather than the test: no condition in the DOM tells a test the effects have run, and the reset could also drop a fast user's first typing.

**Next**
- Inputs in six other files reset their text in a `useEffect` on their value (`forms/scalars.tsx`, `forms/StructEditor.tsx`, `studios/structures/pickers.tsx`, `studios/controls/parts.tsx`, `studios/blocks-items/parts.tsx`, `components/ai/AiLimitsPopover.tsx`); those that commit on blur can lose typing the same way and could take the same pattern.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — effect-reset inputs moved to the render-time reset

**What**
- The seven inputs that reset their text in `useEffect(() => setText(value), [value])` now reset it during render when the value changes (the pattern of `IdInput`): `StringControl` and `NumberControl` (`forms/scalars.tsx`), `KeyInput` (`forms/StructEditor.tsx`, blur-commit), `NumberField` (`studios/structures/pickers.tsx`), `ColourField` (`studios/controls/parts.tsx`), `TextField` (`studios/blocks-items/parts.tsx`), `LimitField` (`components/ai/AiLimitsPopover.tsx`, blur-commit). **Next**

A second pet on the mirrored side works; the runtime must pick the side the parrots leave free each tick.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — B525 spike: fluids, commands, game rules, statistics and events

**What**
- Answered X25–X34 of `docs/PLAN-vanilla-parity-3.md` by observation on 26.3 and 26.4-snapshot-7: a throwaway spike mod in the GameTest source set (`spike5/`, namespace `msm_b525`; 34 GameTests in 9 classes on the GameTest server, one client GameTest on a dedicated server made by `createServer()` with its own port and in singleplayer, headless Mesa EGL) and seven throwaway Mixins in their own config, each with its justification comment. Fluids were registered through the runtime's own `MsmFluid` seam with a spike `LiquidBlock` that has its own mixing check; cauldrons on vanilla's `LayeredCauldronBlock` and `AbstractCauldronBlock`; a drinkable bottle item; game rules by Fabric's `GameRuleBuilder` and straight into the vanilla `game_rule` registry; three `custom_stat` entries; a command `/b525arg` with one literal per candidate argument type; Fabric's sleep events. Signatures read with `javap` only (no `-c`); vanilla's data files read for the advancement trigger and dialog shapes.
- Kept in `docs/reference/spikes/b525/`: the spike source, the temporary resources and the observations (`server-*.json`, `client-*.json`, the failed structure-argument run as a text note); no screenshots or vanilla files. README line added. Spike code, its `fabric.mod.json` entries, Mixin config and data deleted from `engine-mod/`; the fluid tag files restored; `./gradlew build` green on 26.3 and with `-Pmc=26.4` (771 GameTests each).

**Decisions**
- X25 go: our liquid block's own check in `onPlace` and `neighborChanged` mixes identically on both versions (source and flowing blocks, fizz level event 1501, project fluid ids and the vanilla tags). To replace vanilla's 26.3-only obsidian for a lava-like fluid, the block must not call `super` there and schedules the fluid tick itself (measured: no obsidian, the fluid still spreads). Rules naming a fluid id must be checked before rules naming a tag (a water-like project fluid is in `#minecraft:water`). Vanilla lava next to a water-like project fluid still makes obsidian on both versions.
- X26 go without a Mixin: `CauldronInteraction.Dispatcher.put` is package-private, so a project cauldron overrides `useItemOn` and calls vanilla's public `CauldronInteractions.fillBucket`/`emptyBucket`; vanilla's empty cauldron takes a project bucket or bottle through `UseBlockCallback` (reflection into the empty map also works but is not needed).
- X27 go: vanilla's glass bottle gives a water bottle from any fluid in `#minecraft:water`, so the project bottle needs a `UseItemCallback` before vanilla; the bottle is a plain item with a drinking `Consumable`, `usingConvertsTo` glass bottle.
- X28: vanilla boats float on water-like project fluids on both versions (same height, `IN_WATER`); on 26.4 a pushed boat stopped about 0.8 blocks sooner near the edge of the source area (a guide line, no change needed). X29: a resource pack replacing the PNGs at the fluid's texture paths does change the pictures (ADR 0099's finding is only right for packs that re-point the block model).
- X30: 32 argument types work on both versions and reach the client's tree, rebuilt on `/reload`; a `ResourceArgument` over a registry clients do not get (structures) disconnects every client, so structures use `ResourceKeyArgument` or `ResourceOrTagKeyArgument`.
- X31, X32, X34 go without a Mixin. X33: sleeping and waking by Fabric's `EntitySleepEvents`; crafting (`ItemStack.onCraftedBy`), picking up (`ItemEntity.playerTouch`, head and return), eating (`Consumable.onConsume`) and advancements (`PlayerAdvancements.award` head with `AdvancementRewards.grant` head) need Mixins: Fabric has no events for them.

**Next**
- Main session: copy the report's "Notes for the plan" into the plan and ADRs 0108 and 0111 (amendments), then B526.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — B528 runtime: villagers 2

**What**
- Reputation on project traders (ADR 0107 D1 as amended after B524): new `registry/mob/TraderReputation` keeps, per trader and per player, a hit part (`hurt` each, at most 200), a trade part (`trade` each, at most 25) and a gift part (`gift` each, at most 25), saved with the mob (`Reputation`, `ReputationDay`). A player's hit counts through Fabric's `ServerLivingEntityEvents.AFTER_DAMAGE` (registered once, when the first trader with `reputation` is built); a trade counts in `notifyTrade`; a plain use with the gift item gives it (one item taken, happy particles; at the cap the click opens the menu instead). Each clock day hits recover `decay_per_day` and trades fade by 2; gifts do not fade. `MobTrader` sets every offer's special price for the player who opens the menu (minus the value times the offer's multiplier, rounded down, or minus the value divided by `price_step`) and resets it when the menu closes, so each player sees their own prices.
- Demand (D2): each restock runs `updateDemand()` before `resetUses()` when `demand` is on (the default), vanilla's rule as B524 measured it; `demand: false` keeps prices flat.
- Work sites (D3): with `work_site` a due restock only marks the offers as waiting (`restockPending`, saved); new `goals/RestockAtWorkSiteGoal` (added on the mob's first server AI step) looks for the nearest matching block or tagged block within 16 blocks in loaded chunks every 2 seconds, walks there and restocks within 2 blocks; without a site the offers stay used up.
- Project beds as homes (D4 as amended): both `PoiTypes` seams gain `addHome(Block)`, which puts the bed's head states into vanilla's `PoiTypes.TYPE_BY_STATE` with the holder of the red bed's head; `MsmBedBlock` calls it in its constructor (registration time, before any world loads) and warns once if it fails.
- Villager types (D5): `VillagerTypes.register` calls `VillagerTypeParser.parseAll`, registers one `VillagerType` per definition and adds its biome ids to `VillagerType.BY_BIOME` by reflection; biome tags are resolved at `SERVER_STARTING` and after each data pack reload (a reload first puts back what the last resolution replaced), and biome ids or tags the world lacks are warned about then. `DefinitionScanner` reads the kind by `VillagerTypeParser.KIND`.
- GameTests: `MsmTrader2GameTest` 7 (a hit's prices for that player only, trades and gifts to their caps, saving and daily fading, `price_step`, demand up and down and off, restocking at a work site, waiting without one, a villager claiming and sleeping in a project bed) and `MsmVillagerTypeGameTest` 3 (registration and biome map, spawning and breeding spawns in a biome by id and by tag, saving, vanilla's zombie conversion and a golden apple cure keeping the type). New fixtures `trader_market`, `trader_stepped`, `trader_worker`, `trader_idler`, the trade set `msm_test:tr_market/level_1`, `vt_blossom`, `vt_marsh`, `vt_lost`, `vt_zdupe`, two test environments (`b528_day`, `b528_normal`).

**Decisions**
- The standing is saved by `MobTrader` with the mob's own data, not in a Fabric attachment as the amendment suggested: it needs no new init wiring in `MsmRuntime`, and removing `msm:trader` drops it, as ADR 0107's consequences say and as the trading levels do.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — B529 runtime: fluids 2 (mixing, cauldrons, bottles)

**What**
- Mixing (ADR 0108 D1 as amended after B525): `registry/fluid/FluidMixing` holds the rules of every fluid with `mixing`, looked up at `SERVER_STARTING` (an unknown block leaves that side out, an unknown fluid or the fluid itself drops the rule, one warning each, `FluidMixing.lateWarnings()`). `MsmLiquidBlock` overrides `onPlace` and `neighborChanged`: with rules it runs only its own check (the five neighbours other than below; fluid-id rules before `water`/`lava` rules, each in file order; liquids compared by their legacy block) and otherwise schedules the fluid tick itself, so vanilla's 26.3 obsidian rule never runs for it; without rules both stay vanilla's. A match sets the rule's `source` or `flowing` block with `LevelEvent.LAVA_FIZZ`. Falling: both `MsmFluid` seams override `spreadTo`, so the fluid flowing down into a liquid a rule names turns that block into the rule's `flowing` block (vanilla's lava into water).
- Cauldrons (D2, no Mixin): new `MsmCauldronBlock` (sealed; `Layered` on vanilla's `LayeredCauldronBlock` for `levels` on water-like or `none` fluids, `Full` on `AbstractCauldronBlock` otherwise and always for lava-like), both with an empty `CauldronInteraction.Dispatcher`, vanilla's cauldron loot table (drops a cauldron), pick as a cauldron, light from the fluid, no rain or dripstone filling. `MsmCauldrons.register` registers `<ns>:<path>_cauldron` and `<ns>:<path>_bottle`, logs `registered N fluid cauldron(s) and M fluid bottle(s)`, adds clash and unknown-effect errors to the report, and installs one `UseBlockCallback` (project buckets into vanilla's empty, water and lava cauldrons; project bottles into vanilla's empty cauldron for a layered fluid) and one `UseItemCallback` (a glass bottle on a source of a fluid with a bottle). On a project cauldron: the empty bucket takes a full one (`CauldronInteractions.fillBucket`), any bucket with a cauldron (project, vanilla water or lava) replaces the contents (`emptyBucket`), the glass bottle takes a level (`LayeredCauldronBlock.lowerFillLevel`) and the fluid's bottle adds one. Sneaking with an item and spectators skip both callbacks. Inside: a water-like layered cauldron puts fire out and uses a level (vanilla's layered behaviour), a full one applies the fluid's own effects (lava-like ignites and hurts), and both fire `on_entity_inside` under the liquid block's cooldown.
- Bottles (D3): new `MsmBottleItem`, a `Consumable` drink (1.6 s, drink animation and sound, no particles, the effects; food only when given, else `minecraft:consumable` alone), `usingConvertsTo` the glass bottle, stacks of 16, in vanilla's Food and Drinks tab; `finishUsingItem` fires `bottle.on_drink` (self the drinker) after vanilla's food and effects.
- `MsmRegistrar.checkEvents` is public and `MsmFluids.register` runs it for every registered fluid's events (the HANDOFF follow-up).
- Tests: `MsmFluid2GameTest` 18 (replacing the placeholder): registration, seven mixing pairs (source and flowing, placed either way round, project water-like as `water`, id before tag, a water-like fluid's `lava` rule, a rule with an unknown side), no vanilla mixing with rules set, the old per-version behaviour without rules, falling into water, the layered and full cauldrons by bucket and bottle with comparator levels, sneaking, entities inside, a glass bottle on three sources, and a drink to the end with `on_drink` (plus one broken off). Test fluids `mix_lava`, `mix_goo`, `mix_strict`, `plain_pot` with their block states and fluid tags. 796 GameTests per variant.

**Decisions**
- Rule order is global: every id rule (in file order, each over the five sides) before every tag rule; a rule without the needed side does not match that block.
- Buckets replace cauldron contents across liquids as vanilla's cauldrons do among themselves; powder snow is left out (its empty sound is a `SoundEvent` on 26.3 and a holder on 26.4).
- Bottles stack to 16 (honey bottle-like) and cauldrons use vanilla's cauldron loot table, so the lowering needs no loot table for them.

**Next**
- B531 lowers the cauldron's states and models (`level` 1 to 3 on a layered one, none on a full one), the bottle's item model and the companions' names, and adds the cauldrons to `#minecraft:cauldrons`. The spectator skip is an in-game check (the GameTest mock player is never a spectator). `DevFilesTest`'s fluid exception stays: fluids still need an overlay route in `EventOverlay` (not this brief's file).

The catalogue goes from 56 triggers, 44 steps, 19 conditions, 13 values and 7 places to 62, 47, 21, 14 and 7.
- Format: `rules.mcdoc` gains the ids and nine types (`PlayerItemTrigger`, `PlayerAdvancementTrigger`, `CommandArgumentValue`, `GameRuleValue`, `GameRuleCondition`, `StatAtLeastCondition`, `OpenDialogStep`, `AddToStatStep`, `SetGameRuleStep`); `symbols.json` regenerated (582 types).
- Compiler: the checker takes a `CheckContext` (the subject command's arguments, the kinds of project game rules). A typed argument must be one of the command's, of a type Rules reads (`READABLE_ARGUMENT_TYPES`: integer and number as numbers, position and block position by axis, word, text, player, entity, item, block, dimension and effect as words; limit N20), and a number where a number is needed (`rules.unknown-value`, `rules.not-a-number`, `rules.not-for-trigger`; no new codes). A boolean project game rule takes only true or false, an integer one only numbers, and true or false compares only with "equal to". The script reads the arguments from the event in both routes (the command's own event through `run_script`, and the `command` listener of a command with a function) with `commandArgs(e)`, declared only in handlers that read them; helpers `argNumber`, `argWords` (a player argument by name), `gameRuleNumber`.

- "Open a dialog" compiles to script (`Player.openDialog`): `action.mcdoc` has no `open_dialog` action yet, so a plain-rule route would fail the definition schema.
- The new triggers sit in the "players" group; game rule, statistic and advancement ids are plain strings in the format (no registry check), the dialog id is checked against the `dialog` registry.
