## 2026-11-22 — executor — B532 runtime: mobs 2

**What**
- Fish buckets (ADR 0109 D1 as amended): every body (`MsmEntity`, `MsmAnimal`, `MsmMonster`, so the GeckoLib and storage bodies too) implements vanilla's `Bucketable` and hands it to `MobBuckets`. `MobBuckets.itemFor` registers `<ns>:<path>_bucket` for a `swim` mob with `msm:bucketable`: vanilla's `MobBucketItem` with water (stacks to 1, empty `bucket_entity_data`), or `MobBuckets.DryBucketItem` with `water: false` (an empty bucket takes the mob, using it on a block puts the mob on that face and gives the bucket back); `item_name` overrides the name; Tools and Utilities tab. The bucket keeps vanilla's default data plus the variant id (`Variant`); a released mob is "from a bucket" (saved `FromBucket`, never despawns). The bucket comes before feeding in `mobInteract`.
- Both shoulders (D2 as amended): sides are named by the player's view; the old offset is the right (`MobShoulder.offset(owner)` = `offset(owner, Side.RIGHT)`), the left is its mirror. `sides` left/right/either (either takes the right first); two pets per player (`PERCHED` holds two seats); a side holding a vanilla parrot is not free and every tick a pet moves to the side the parrots leave free, or gets off. New synched `MsmAnimal.DATA_PERCH_LEFT`, saved `PerchSide`. The class documentation now says right, not left.
- Flight (D3): `hover` uses `MobMovement.HoverMoveControl` (vanilla's flying control at the mob's own height, then a damped climb or sink to `hover_height` over the first collision shape or liquid surface below; the wanted height only while it has a target). `phase`: `PhaseChargeGoal` replaces the melee goal (flies straight at the target's eyes, hits on contact, 20-tick cooldown), and `MobMovement.tick` runs vanilla's tick with `noPhysics` while charging and until the mob is out of the block. `swoop` is `SwoopGoal` (circles 6 blocks round a point `height` over the target for 60 to 120 ticks, dives at twice the speed, hits, climbs back). `roost` is `RoostGoal` (by day or `when_idle`; hangs under a sturdy underside with the box's top at it; lets go when hurt, targeting, a player within 4 blocks, the block gone or the day over; 100-tick cooldown).
- Habits (D4): `MobHabits` holds the state (saved `Roosting`, `PlayDeadTicks`, `CollectLiked`, `CollectCarried`, `CollectOwner`, `DigCooldown`, `BarterHeld`, `BarterTicks`; what it holds drops on death) and the goals `CollectItemsGoal` (given an item by a click, fetches the same item, skips items it threw, delivers to a note block heard in the last 30 s through its own game event listener, else to the owner; an empty hand takes the item back), `DigForItemsGoal` (walks to the nearest dig block within 8, digs 40 ticks, rolls `loot_table` in the gift context), `PlayDeadGoal` (priority 0 by default; hurt below `below_health`: still, not seen as an enemy, Regeneration I for `ticks`), `BarterGoal` (from the ground; from a hand by a click; rolls in the barter context with the mob only after `ticks`).
- Dash (D4): `MobRiding` charges the bar into a dash when `dash` is set (1.6 x `power` x scale forward, 0.3 x scale up, in `tickRidden` where the mob is moved), `handleStartJump` starts the server's cooldown, `getJumpCooldown` shows it on vanilla's bar.
- Synched flags (D5): `DATA_ROOSTING` and `DATA_PLAYING_DEAD` on each body (`MsmMob.roostingData()`, `playingDeadData()`); `MsmVanillaRenderer.extractRenderState` draws roosting upside down (`isUpsideDown`) and playing dead fallen over (`deathTime` 20); a `fly`-like `hover` or `phase` mob counts as flying for the pose. GeckoLib renderers are not changed.
- Tests: `MsmMob2GameTest` 13 (replacing the placeholder) in the new `mob2_yard` structure with 13 `mob2_*` test definitions; `MsmMobStorageGameTest`'s one-pet test became `damageOrLeavingTakesThePetsOffAndTwoSitAtMost`; `MsmEntityGameTest` counts `mob2_` among the feature definitions; client `MsmMobs2ClientGameTest` (hover height, roosting and playing dead flags and render states, screenshot `msm_mobs2_hover_roost_dead_<mc>`). 817 GameTests per variant: `./gradlew build` on 26.3 and 26.4, `runGameTest -PwithoutGeckolib`, client GameTests on both versions.

**Decisions**
- Hover treats a liquid's surface as ground (a ghast-like mob over the sea does not sink to the sea bed); the spike's controller bobbed (1.3 to 8 blocks), so the height is set as a share of the error each tick instead.
- A collector keeps the given item in its own saved field rather than in its hand (no equipment drop chances), as does the barterer.
- The habits' searches count canUse calls rather than `tickCount % n`, since the goal selector does not ask a waiting goal every tick.
- Left `RestockAtWorkSiteGoal` in `MobTrader` (moving it was optional).

**Next**
- Parity cases (B541), Try it (B540), Studio fields (B538), guide (B543). Dashing has no synched pose flag (no renderer needs it yet).

- The worker's messages are app-local envelopes around the engine's protocol: `TerrainRequest` for samples and cancels and `TerrainAnswer` inside `answer`, plus `vanilla` (files once per key), a `world` message carrying the seed as typed (the worker calls `seedFromText`, so the conversion stays the engine's) and a `world` summary and `error` answer, which `TerrainAnswer` has no form for. `api.ts` is unchanged.
- `filesHash` in requests carries the world's hash (files, vanilla key, facts, source and seed). For `heights`, `fn` names the height map (`'surface'` by default). A `columns` request without a stage builds `terrain`.

- Tests live in `app/test/components/terrain/` rather than `app/test/terrain/`: renderer tests are type-checked by `tsconfig.web.json`, which includes `test/components` only, and the tsconfigs are not this brief's files.
- Lowered elements are keyed by kind and id (a dimension and its noise settings share an id); an element is lowered again only when its data differs, not merely its object.

- deepslate's own `mapAll` maps a named function again at every reference, so `sloped_cheese` (read three times a corner) was three nodes: `NoiseBinder` resolves each name once. With the per-column cache (every part that does not depend on y, the parts inside it too) the router stays bit-identical to deepslate's: checked on all 7 noise settings of both jars (`Object.is` at 400+ points each), and `ChunkFill` equals deepslate's `doFill` on a chunk, aquifers included.
- deepslate gives `NoiseAquifer` the settings' unmapped functions (every noise 0). Binding them changes 3.3 % of the cells below y 100; the spike measured deepslate's route against real worlds, so `BIND_AQUIFER_NOISES` is false and only the names are resolved. B579's parity should try both.
- `MapRegion.width` and `depth` are blocks (as B580 reads them); every function returns fresh arrays.
- Heights leave aquifers out (the land's shape and the sea) and match a block by block search exactly; found heights are kept per world for panning.
- The extension entry shapes live in `parser.ts` and `rules.ts` (`DensityFunctionType`, `RuleType`, `ConditionType`) and `world.ts` (`FlatGeneratorFn`); `extensions/index.ts` is B581's and was not edited.

**Measured (Node, both jars, median, 4 shared cores):** coarse biome map 49 to 54 ms (250 ms); full 256 by 256 biomes 642 to 744 ms (2 s); side cut 256 wide, full height 156 to 161 ms (1 s); ground of 9 chunks 32 high 121 to 170 ms at y 50, 222 to 321 ms at y -20 (1.5 s); 9 full-height chunks 1.0 to 1.1 s; a new world 125 to 133 ms, after an edit that keeps the random state 4 ms. **Height map missed:** 256 by 256 at a 4-block step 15.4 to 16.1 s (2 s), 128 by 128 3.8 to 4.1 s, 64 by 64 1.1 s, 256 by 256 at a 1-block step 8.0 to 8.9 s; the floor is the splines that do not depend on y (about 35 µs a column) plus the base noise at each cell row the bound cannot rule out.

- Verified: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, app tests (297 files, 2811 tests, before the last notes change; terrain and preview tests after it), `@msm/plugin-worldgen` tests, `pnpm build`, `dist:dir`, check-size, e2e `smoke` and `worldgen-path` under `xvfb-run -a`. Measured in the running app under `xvfb-run -a` (scratch spec, not committed; vanilla 26.3 files extracted from the Loom jar through a fake Prism root; the Multi-noise overworld template, an edit of the dimension's `type`): from the project change to the first coarse picture 161 to 231 ms over 16 edits, the 150 ms debounce included (11 to 81 ms after it); Height to done 3.4 to 3.9 s; Side cut 0.83 to 0.88 s.

**Decisions:**

Biomes ask one sample every `max(4, zoom)` blocks.
- Answers are kept raw and coloured while painting, so a project change that only recolours does not ask the worker again; the old picture stays until the new world's first answer.

While it shows, the files are read again every 5 s (a cache made again by itself, B577); a set-up calls `forgetVanillaWorldgen()` and reads again.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — CI fixes: 26.4 library data packs, terrain features timeout

**What:**
- Run 45053570100, engine-mod (26.4), "Export the library's vanilla data packs": `examples/worlds/coral_isles` (and the other four world examples and the five `examples/starters/world-*` mirrors, B586) exported `worldgen/noise_settings/<x>/terrain.json` with `default_block`, which 26.4's schema refuses. Cause: the mirror projects are 26.3 projects (`targets: ["mc-26.3"]`), and the test exported the vanilla-only ones for 26.4 as they are, which the app never does (it exports a project for its own target, after Upgrade project target). And Upgrade project target itself left `default_block` in place, so a real 26.3 project with noise settings moved to 26.4 failed its export the same way. Fix: `mc-26.4`'s `migrateFrom` (`packages/targets/mc-26.4/src/migrate.ts`) now drops `default_block` from noise settings elements and from noise settings written inline in a dimension's or each world preset dimension's `generator.settings`, as one `update` change per element (combined with any renames), driven by the target's own `noiseSettingsDefaultBlock` fact (passed through `migrationTables`, a constant in `target.ts`). The library test (`packages/exporters/test/library.test.ts`, `upgraded`) moves a mirror project to the selected target as the app's `upgradeTarget` does (migration problems must be none) before exporting it. Reproduced locally with `MSM_TARGET_ID=mc-26.4`: failing on coral_isles before, passing after (390 packs on 26.4, 428 on 26.3; coral_isles' noise settings have `default_block` on 26.3 only). Tests: two new cases in `packages/targets/mc-26.4/test/migrate.test.ts` (elements, inline dimension and world preset settings, ids left alone, a target with the field keeps it).
- ci job: `@msm/terrain` `test/features.test.ts` › "gives the same placements for the same seed and others for another" timed out at 5 s on CI (5.24 s; 0.76 to 0.93 s locally). Real repeated work: `build` made the surface grid for every world although most tests read only the features. It now builds each stage when first read, which halves that test alone (0.33 to 0.42 s). The three describes also get an explicit 30 s timeout with the measurements in a comment, since CI ran about 5.7 times slower than this machine and two other tests reach 0.85 s with the whole suite running. Every other terrain test above 1.5 s locally (parity, vanilla, features-vanilla) already has an explicit timeout; the rest stay under 0.55 s.
- Verified: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `@msm/target-mc-26.4` (126), `@msm/targets` (74), `@msm/plugin-worldgen` (191), `@msm/terrain` (139), `@msm/plugin-library` (2211), `@msm/exporters` (1995), the library data pack step for both targets, app `session-targets` and `main-menu` tests.

**Decisions:**
- Fixed in the migration rather than in the worldgen plugin's lowering: ADR 0036 D8 keeps noise settings data per target (no data is valid on both, and the editor validates the element's own data, so a lowering that quietly dropped or added `default_block` would leave the element showing an error and would have to invent a block on 26.3), and moving a project between targets is `migrateFrom`'s job (ADR 0037 D3, D4). The examples cannot carry data both targets accept.
- The migration drops the field whenever this target has none, not only when the previous target had it, so a stand-in previous target in tests behaves as the real one.

**Next:** ADR 0037 D3 could note that `migrateFrom` also reshapes noise settings (the orchestrator's call). The test still skips mod mirror projects on a non-default target ("noise settings fields of the default target" was one reason); with the migration in place they could be tried on 26.4.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — B592 the vanilla biome list from the runtime's dev mode

**What:**
- Runtime: new `engine-mod/src/main/java/dev/mcsupermods/runtime/dev/DevBiomeLists.java`. In dev mode only (`DevMode.current()` set: a client's integrated server with a valid `msm-dev/dev.json`, or the GameTest route; never a dedicated server), at `SERVER_STARTED`, it asks vanilla's own accessor `MultiNoiseBiomeSourceParameterList.knownPresets()` (signatures by `javap` only) and writes `<gameDir>/msm-dev/biome-lists.json` (format 1: `format`, `minecraftVersion` = `WorldVersion.id()`, `presets` by preset id with a sorted `biomes` palette and `points` as `[biome index, tMin, tMax, hMin, hMax, cMin, cMax, eMin, eMax, dMin, dMax, wMin, wMax, offset]` in the game's quantized whole numbers, in the list's order). Written atomically and only when the text changed; a failure is logged, never fails the start. 26.3: 7,599 points, 26.4-snapshot-7: 7,600; about 0.7 MB. `DevMode.register()` registers it; `DevMode`'s and the package's comments now name the one file the server side writes.
- GameTest `MsmDevBiomeListsGameTest` (2 tests; `fabric.mod.json` line): dev mode off writes nothing; on, the file equals vanilla's lists point by point with registered biomes, and an unchanged list is not written again; the second test writes `reference.json` (the game's own biome at 3,328 cells for seeds 0, 1, 12345 and -7046235981325167892, overworld at y -32, 64 and 160, the Nether at y 32) beside the lists in the run folder, through the new gametest seam `ClimateReference` (26.3 `RandomState.create`, 26.4 `createForTesting`). 845 GameTests per variant.
- App: `app/src/main/platform/worldgen-biome-lists.ts` reads the file as a save is read (real paths inside the instance's game folder, 8 MB limit, every value checked, the version must equal the target's `mcVersion`, never throws or writes). `app/src/shared/platform.ts`: `ResolvedBiomeListView` and `ResolvedBiomeListsView` get their shape (the IPC schema stays a record). `terrain/files.ts` lays the lists into vanilla's files under `msm/resolved_biome_list` and keys the worker's vanilla files by them; an answer without lists is asked again after 30 s (`BIOME_LISTS_RECHECK_MS`), so a Play made while the app runs shows vanilla's biomes.
- Terrain: `presets.ts` `resolvePreset` turns a list into a `multi_noise` source's points (`RESOLVED_BIOME_LISTS_FOLDER`); `world.ts` makes the noises `minecraft:nether/temperature` and `minecraft:nether/vegetation` the old Nether way under `legacy_random_source` (deepslate does it only for the old ids), learned by observation: the Nether's cells went from 68 to 250 of 256.
- End to end (scratch test, not committed): the GameTest's file copied into a game folder's `msm-dev/`, read by `readResolvedBiomeLists`, laid in as `files.ts` does, drawn by the engine over the Loom client jar's files. 26.3: overworld 3,072 of 3,072 cells the game's biome (exact), the Nether 250 of 256 (97.7 %; the misses sit at borders); a 2,048-block map of seed 0 shows 20 biomes, of seed 12345 35. 26.4-snapshot-7: the same counts. The repeatable check is `TERRAIN_BIOME_LISTS=<run folder> pnpm --filter @msm/terrain exec vitest run test/presets.test.ts`.
- Guide `live-world.md` and the AI prompt now say the biomes show after a Play. The notes "Vanilla's biomes show here after you have pressed Play once." in `WorldMap.tsx`, `CompareView.tsx` and `tryit/grounds.ts` are now true and unchanged.
- Verified: `./gradlew build` (26.3), `-Pmc=26.4` and `-PwithoutGeckolib`: 845 of 845 each; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`; terrain (142, 7 skipped), interop (185), ai (111) and app (309 files, 2,919) tests.

**Decisions:**
- No version seam for the writer: `knownPresets()`, `ParameterList`, `ParameterPoint` and `WorldVersion.id()` have the same signatures on both versions (`javap`), and the engine's rule is that a call compiling on every version needs none. The seam is the GameTest's climate sampler, which differs.
- B574 compared no vanilla overworld biomes (WS9), so the end-to-end check compares with the game's own sampler and list at the same cells; the GameTest world's levels are not `multi_noise`, so they could not be used.
- The lists go to the engine through vanilla's file map, not a new engine input, so `api.ts` is unchanged.

**Next:** the Nether's last 2.3 % (borders; the lookup near borders is already about right, B581); `engine-mod/CLAUDE.md` (`dev/` gains `DevBiomeLists`, 845 GameTests) at the close; on 26.4 the layout stays labelled WL17.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — offline checker: score holders and names declared in the function

**What**
- Cause: MSM's wrapper parsed a function with the bare `mcfunction` entry parser, whose root node has no local symbol table (Spyglass's own `core.file` wrapper adds one). Spyglass's `VanillaConfig` `undeclaredSymbol` rule declares every name it cannot otherwise place (score holders like `#a`, named random sequences, `place jigsaw` target names, and ids in a non-`minecraft` namespace such as a project's block or particle) with `block` visibility, which needs a node with `locals`, so the linter threw "Cannot enter ... with Block visibility as no node with locals is supplied". Not a Spyglass bug: MSM's own entry code. `scoreboard players set #a` passed only because it is a declaration usage.
- Fix in `packages/schemas/src/mcfunction/service.ts`: the parse step gives the root node `locals` as `core.file` does. The check never throws now: binding and checking, each linter rule, and the parse are guarded; a Spyglass exception becomes one `info` problem ("The function checker stopped early ...") and the stages that ran keep their problems. Completion returns nothing instead of throwing.
- Tests: `packages/targets/mc-26.{3,4}/test/mcfunction-holders.test.ts` (every case of `docs/reference/spikes/b547/results/spyglass-holders.txt`, random `roll` and `reset`, `place jigsaw`, a project block and particle, all at once, a wrong line still an error, an undeclared objective still a warning, completion after a holder; 14 of 20 fail without the fix); `packages/schemas/test/mcfunction/never-throws.test.ts` (a holder on a hand-written tree; a forced Spyglass throw becomes one info problem and keeps the other errors). All 47 functions in `fixtures/` and `examples/` checked on both targets: before, `sample-machines` `place_loot_crate` and `sample-particles` `burst` threw; after, nothing throws and no new error appears. The library's sources have no other such lines. `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, schemas, both target and app mcfunction tests pass; e2e `datapack-path` passes.

**Decisions**
- A checker exception is an `info`, not a warning or error, so it never blocks an export or fills Things to fix for a line the game accepts.

**Next**
- `projectIds.team` is namespaced like a resource location (`t` becomes `minecraft:t`), so a project-wide team never matches `team join t`; teams (like objectives) are plain names. Small follow-up in `service.ts` `projectIdsKey`/`applyProjectIds` if the app ever passes teams.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — Structure templates placed as air (B547 Y12 fix)

**What**
- Cause confirmed in the game: `structureTemplateToNbt` wrote every palette entry as `{Name, Properties}` with the target's own `DataVersion` (5023, 5127). The 26.3 and 26.4-snapshot-7 dedicated servers load such a file ("Loaded template") but read every entry as no block, so every MSM-exported template (data packs, content jars, the Java eject, `.nbt` exports) placed as air. Measured with one-block `oak_log[axis=x]` templates written both ways at every data version 4990 to 5127 and every 25th from 4100, placed and read back with `execute if block`: `Name` places up to 5005 and is air from 5006 on, on both versions; `id`/`properties` places at every data version tried.
- Fix (`packages/plugins/structures/src/nbt/structure-template.ts`): `ID_PALETTE_DATA_VERSION = 5006` and `paletteKeys(dataVersion)`; the writer uses `id`/`properties` from 5006 on and `Name`/`Properties` below it. The reader still takes both forms and bare strings, so old files import. Both exported from the plugin's index. `.schem` (block-state strings) is unaffected.
- In-game proof in CI: `tools/run-fabric-server/vanilla-templates.ts` (with `vanilla-templates.test.ts`, README section) puts the sample worldgen data zip on a vanilla dedicated server, places its three templates with `place template` and reads all 150 blocks back with `execute if block`, the expected blocks taken from the elements. `sample-worldgen.golden.test.ts` writes the zip and `template-facts.json` with `MSM_SAMPLE_WORLDGEN_OUT`; two new steps in the `engine-mod` CI job (both matrix versions) and the log in the artefact. Before the fix: 0 of 122 non-air blocks on 26.3 and on 26.4 (only the 28 air blocks passed); after: 150 of 150 on both. No earlier test had placed a template in the game (the goldens only read the files back with our own codec).
- Re-pinned: `packages/plugins/structures/test/fixtures/mc-26.{3,4}/expected/structure/hut.nbt` (the golden test now also asserts `id` and no `Name` on every target), `packages/exporters/test/fixtures/mc-26.{3,4}/sample-worldgen-data.sha256`, `app/e2e/assets/sample-piece.nbt` (regenerated by its script). The `examples/` mirror and `fixtures/sample-*` hold templates as element JSON (block-state strings), which did not change; no other golden carries a template.
- Docs: targets' `CHANGES.md` (both) record the fact and its evidence beside `dataVersion`; ADR 0021 D1 gets a dated note; `fixtures/sample-worldgen/README.md`; CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` Fixed.
- Verified: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, structures (74), exporters (1,995), targets (242, 126, 74), library (2,211), worldgen (191), tools run-fabric-server (76), app (314 files, 2,944 tests); the in-game check on both versions before and after.

**Decisions**
- The palette key form is decided inside the plugin by the existing `dataVersion` fact, not by a new target field: no plugin API change (1.21.0 stays; 1.22.0 and 1.23.0 are reserved). It is honest because the game itself switches the format by the file's data version (older files are upgraded), so the boundary is a property of the file format, measured, and every target's own data version picks the right form; a future target below 5006 would get `Name` correctly.
- The check uses a vanilla server and `place template` rather than a parity GameTest: templates are plain data, and the same console route B547 used needs no Fabric or Gradle build.

**Next**
- B551 (start island by `place template`) and B552 (area resets) can rely on exported templates now.
- In game by hand: `fixtures/sample-worldgen/README.md` (a) and (b) on the user's machine, since the hamlet never generated with blocks before this fix.

## 2026-11-22 — executor — The community repository: tools/check-project and tools/community-repo

**What**
- The user's request ("make another repo where we store all our public example mod or people created mods"; chosen: examples and submissions). New repository [MCSuperMods-Community](https://github.com/MEZTKING/MCSuperMods-Community): `examples/` (all 87 mirror projects, each with `picture.png` and a README from the library entry), `mods/` for people's own mods by pull request (`mods/_template/`), README, CONTRIBUTING, MIT `LICENSE` with the licence rules (mods state their own; CC BY 4.0 when none), a pull request checklist and `.github/workflows/check.yml`.
- `tools/check-project/`: `node tools/check-project/index.ts <folder>... [--target <id>|all] [--json]`. Runs the app's own `ProjectSession` (built-in plugins and targets, the main process's mcfunction broker and scripting service) over an in-memory copy of each folder: Upgrade project target (`upgradeTargetPreview`, `upgradeTarget`) when the target is not the project's own, every validator, the resource pack and data pack zips and the Fabric mod jar (`separateRuntime`). Says which exports the content needs (the layers of its lowered files). File rules: only project files plus README, LICENSE and picture.png; nothing under `assets/minecraft/`; no export shipping `assets/minecraft/textures|sounds`; no picture or sound whose name nothing mentions; PNG and Ogg signatures; 2 MiB a file, 8 MiB a sound, 25 MiB a folder.
- `tools/community-repo/sync.ts --repo <checkout> [--check]`: writes the community `examples/` (project files byte for byte, the first non-empty item or block texture enlarged to 128 px without smoothing or a drawn placeholder, a README, `examples/README.md` by category); idempotent; `--check` fails when out of date.
- `tools/shared/workspace-hooks.ts`: `module.registerHooks` resolves the workspace's imports without endings and Vite's `?raw`, so both tools run under plain Node 24.
- Checked: all 87 examples pass on mc-26.4 and mc-26.3 (from the mirror and from the community copies); `pnpm lint`, tools typecheck and the tools' tests (28 new) pass.

**Decisions**
- The checker reuses the app's session rather than copying the library test's export helpers, so it exports exactly as the app does; `@msm/tools` may depend on anything (`layers.json`), and its tsconfig now references `app/tsconfig.node.json`.
- No exporter rule against Mojang assets exists, so the rule is the checker's own and conservative (documented in its README); the "asset nothing uses" rule matches names, not bytes, because the packs copy every asset.
- A community example is its mirror folder's path with the project at the folder's top; submissions use the same layout under `mods/<name>/`.

**Next**
- After a change to the examples mirror, run the sync into a checkout of the community repository and commit there; its CI fails until then.
- The main session pushes the community repository's first commit and checks its first workflow run (`pnpm/action-setup` `package_json_file` and the checkout paths: verify at implementation).

## 2026-11-22 — executor — B680 the AI helper's run engine: waits, failures, limits and prices

**What**
- `@msm/ai` only (ADR 0125 D2, D8, D9, D10, D12). The scripted model gains `delayMs` on a turn (nothing is emitted before it; the abort signal ends the wait) and error turns `{ "error": { "errorClass", "message", "status" } }` that throw a `ModelClientError`, plus `cacheCreation1hInputTokens` in a turn's usage.
- Failures: `classifyModelClientError` works out one of `AI_ERROR_CLASSES` from the status and the API's error type before the SDK class (402 or `billing_error` is `BillingError`, 529 or `overloaded_error` `OverloadedError`, 413 `RequestTooLargeError`, the SDK's time-out, 408 and 504 `TimeoutError`); `describeModelClientError` says a plain sentence from `ERROR_SENTENCES` without the class name (Anthropic's own text is kept only after a refused request and an unknown failure). The `done` event gains `errorClass` (also `ContextWindowExceeded`, `ModelOutputError` and `Error` from the loop).
- Limits: the limit stop says 'The helper paused at its limit so the cost stays small; send "continue" to carry on.' with no numbers; `done` carries `limit: { toolTurns, outputTokens }`. A `propose_plan` answer of `build_all` or `step` raises the run's limits to the larger of its own and the settings' build limits (`raisedLimits`, `acceptsPlan`); the effort stays the run's, so the cache holds.
- Cache: the system block is cached for an hour (`SYSTEM_CACHE_TTL = '1h'`, the one-line veto); the conversation's top-level breakpoint keeps five minutes, so the longer entry comes first. The pinned SDK (1.1.0) types `ttl?: '5m' | '1h'`. Usage counts one-hour writes from `usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`.
- Prices, read on 2026-11-22 from https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing: Opus 5.5 $4 / $20, cache hits $0.20; Sonnet 5.5 $2 / $10, cache hits $0.10 (was $0.20 here); Haiku 5.5 $0.10 / $0.50, cache hits $0.01, and over 100,000 prompt tokens $0.50 / $2.50, cache hits $0.05; writes 1.25 times input for five minutes and 2 times for an hour; 286 tool-use system tokens on all three. New `typicalCost(model, prefixTokens)` (a first question and a follow-up), `PROMPT_PREFIX_CHARS` (112,804: the build prompt 90,470 plus the tools 22,334, held within 5 % by a test), `PROMPT_PREFIX_TOKENS` (28,487 at four characters a token, an estimate).
- Tests: new `errors.test.ts`; new cases in `scripted-client.test.ts`, `loop.test.ts` and `models.test.ts`. `@msm/ai` 128 green; app `main-ai-service`, `ai-scenario`, `ai-art-scenario`, `ai-rules`, `ai-patterns`, `ai-store`, `main-e2e-hooks` and the AI component tests green unchanged; `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` green.

**Decisions**
- The error class is a classification, not always the SDK's name: the SDK has no class for 402 and reports 529 as `InternalServerError`, and `src/sdk/index.ts` is not this brief's, so billing and overloaded are found from the status and from the error type in the message text.
- Haiku 5.5's higher tier is decided per request; a summed usage is priced as `requests` requests of its average prompt (exact for one request, an estimate for a sum).
- The typical question assumes 2,000 tokens of message and conversation and 1,500 of answer, one request (`TYPICAL_QUESTION`): on Opus 5.5 about $0.27 for a first question and $0.05 for a follow-up; Sonnet 5.5 $0.13 and $0.02; Haiku 5.5 under a cent.

- `components/ai/ai-words.ts` (new, D13): every word of the wording table by mode (`wordsFor`, `statusWords`, `noticeWords`, `appliedWords`, `doneSentence`, `planLineWords`, `closedPlanWords`, `reviewHeading`, `explainChip`, `costSentence`, the four `EXAMPLE_ASKS`), `toolLine(message, mode)` beside today's `toolSummary` (words for `checkpoint` and `note_missing_feature`; `null` for the lines Very easy and Easy hide), the failure table by error class, and `VERY_EASY_FORBIDDEN` with `forbiddenIn`.
- `store/ai-store.ts`: a plan is a `plan` entry of the transcript where it was proposed (mirrored into the deprecated `conversation.plan`), closed to one line once its run has ended; `tickedItemIds` ticks a line only when the changes or the project hold its element; runs take their size from the caller (`startRun(…, size)`), record `startedAt`, `turnStartedAt`, `userSeq`, and keep `errorClass`, `limit` and `stopDetails`; notices carry them too, and an Apply notice carries its step; `typedPlanDecision` ("go", "yes", "ok" build all, else revise with the text), `typedStepDecision`, `tryAgainRequest`, `keepGoingRequest`; `doneNotice` says plain words (no more "The run failed: …" or "The run stopped at its limit.").
- `ai-controller.ts`: `send(…, { size })`, `answer`, `awaitsAnswer`, `tryAgain`, `keepGoing`; typed text answers a waiting plan or step; `apply()` returns the things made and the undo label, and its notice follows Undo and Redo ("Undone.", then today's text again); the draft can carry a size. `ai/project-context.ts` adds `view`, `modName` and `open`.
- Tests: new `ai-status.test.ts` (2,160 combinations of run, plan, step, changes and last notice: one line, at most one action, never working while the answer is awaited), new `ai-words.test.ts` (every Very easy string swept), `ai-store.test.ts` cases; `ai-fixtures.ts` gains `aiStateFixtures()`, one conversation per state.

**Decisions**
- Honest ticks are a function (`tickedItemIds`, `tickedLines`) rather than a filter on `completed`, because today's panel test (`ai-panel.test.tsx`, not this brief's) ticks a line the changes do not hold; B686 draws ticks through `tickedLines`.
- The notice's stored `text` stays today's words (component tests and e2e `ai-path` read them); the words per mode come from `noticeWords`.
- `ai-status.ts`, `ai-words.ts` and `preview/bundle-source.ts` are added to `app/tsconfig.node.json`, since the store and the Node tests reach them; for that reason `ai-words.ts` keeps its own copy of My things' kinds (`THING_KIND_WORDS`), held equal to `home/things.ts` by a test.

**Next**
- B685 draws the state line from `conversationStatus` and `statusWords`, the plan entries in place, notices through `noticeWords`, tool lines through `toolLine`; B686 the plan with `planLineWords`, `closedPlanWords`, `tickedLines` and the cost with `costSentence`; B688 replaces `thingsOf` with its `proposal-things.ts`; B689 calls `send(…, { size: 'build' })` instead of `setMode`.

**Decisions**
- The plugin's `load` and `tick` are function tags, not functions: lowering sees one element at a time and only tags and flat objects merge (`OutputFile.merge`). `function #<ns>:msm_games/load` runs it like a function.
- "Loads in a vanilla data pack" is tested through schema validation, the mcfunction checker and the merge check inside the games package, since `@msm/exporters` gains its dependency on the games plugin in B551.
- Commands with no form in `TargetFacts.commands.forms` are written as plain text (`execute`, `function`, `tag`, `kill`, `setblock`, `summon`, `tellraw`, and `scoreboard players remove` for the count down, since `players add` takes no negative); all are checked on both targets.

- ADR 0113 D9's refusal of project functions under `msm_games/` is left out: a validator reading `minecraft:function` breaks the app's `session-importers-validators` expectation (not this brief's file).
- Live views (ADR 0119 D1; none built here): `msm:one_block` Try it's one block refilling by phase (B558); `msm:team` team colours and prefixes on names in Try it (B558); `msm:objective` Try it's sidebar or list mock-up (B558); `msm:timer` Try it's boss bar or action bar mock-up (B558); `msm:area` the Area Studio's box over a Try it ground (B555) and Try it's outline with enter and leave (B558).

The stemmer: B650's collision list of 20 empty against the dictionary fixture (B650 left `ranged`/`range`), 750 merged groups (B650 748). Folding idempotent over the list and 20,000 seeded random words. The package's tests 1.1 s in all.

**Decisions**
- The query word is folded before it is corrected (as the query will do): `pickax` folds to `pickaxe`, one more right than B650. `sulfur` is not folded (both spellings are used in British English, and folding it made the misspelling `slufur` unreachable).
- Stemmer changes from the spike, each a fix found by comparing with it over the dictionary: `ranged` joins the exceptions; a plural becomes its dictionary singular before `-ies` is read (`cookies` is `cookie`, not `cooky`), `-es` after x, ch, sh and zz is tried first (`touches` is `touch`); a doubled `l` undoubles (`cancelled`, `travelled` meet `cancel`, `travel`). `lapis` left the exception list (no game word in the code; the rules never strip -is). The other words B650 compared stem as the spike did.
- Intent: D4's cues plus their -ing forms, `whats`, `guide`, `explain`, `remove`, `crash`, `redo`, and the pairs `what is`, `can i`, `not working`; the spike's `pink`, `my`, `turn`, `switch` and `save` were not taken (they would turn ordinary queries into fixes or commands). `no`, `not`, `without`, `on`, `off` and `all` are not stop words.
- `src/index.ts` is unchanged: the text modules are internal to the engine until a brief needs them exported.

**Next**

Consider protecting an id word only when its stem would be another dictionary word, or index both forms. ## 2026-11-23 — executor — B658 search engine: index and ranking

**What**
- `packages/search/src/index/` (ADR 0124 D3, D4): `entry.ts` (an entry's six fields, title, words, question and choice labels, sentence, ids, body, split once into folded words with stop words left out, whole ids and their paths kept beside their words; a fast path for plain ASCII text that gives exactly `tokenise`'s words; `actionKey`, a stable key of an action descriptor); `postings.ts` (a segment: terms by number, postings, per-field counts, field lengths and titles in typed arrays); `layer.ts` (layers built, replaced and patched by deltas: a patch clears live flags and adds one small segment, a layer with more than 8 segments or a quarter dead is rebuilt as one; words counted per entry exactly); `dictionary.ts` (every word of the layers and the vocabulary with its entry count, the B653 stemmer with the protected words in force, stem classes reached at query time, the trigram typo index); `vocabulary.ts` (the plugins' word groups merged by idea across plugins, phrases of several words, the ideas of several words too, misspellings, near words, vanilla ids, colour names).
- `packages/search/src/rank/`: `weights.ts` (every number: field weights and normalisation, the expansion weights, bonuses, coverage, context factors, the intent by source table, source order, the confidence floor, rows), `bm25f.ts` (BM25F weighed at query time over the whole index's statistics), `signals.ts` (intent and lean, availability, Very easy's technical entries, the open mod's kinds, the local history, coverage, exact title or name, every word in the title, words in order and close, a flow that makes the thing named, a behaviour that fits), `fold.ts` (entries with the same action are one result, shown as the source that comes first), `sections.ts` (three Best matches, the sections in the order of their best score with three rows and a count, More last in Very easy, unavailable entries last and never Best, the confidence floor, scopes).
- `packages/search/src/query.ts`: `createSearchIndex(options)` returns a `SearchEngine` (the frozen `SearchIndex` plus `setVocabulary`, `setProtected`, `setAnswerReader`, `setContext`, `warm`, `entry`, `stats`); the words read in B653's order (intent on the words as typed; whole ids; vocabulary phrases and joined and split words before stop words are dropped; each word folded, its stem class reached, its vocabulary group, a listed misspelling read as its idea, the word being typed completed before it is corrected, an unknown word corrected by the typo index); `toSlim`; the seam for B659 (`SearchAnswerReader`: words to leave out of the text score, entries to add, chips, and per entry the answers, the words absorbed, whether it makes the thing named and whether a behaviour fits). `src/index.ts` exports the engine, the weights, the section ids and the vocabulary types; `createSearchIndex` left `types.ts`.
- Tests (130, 2 s without the two heavy ones): one file per module under `test/index/` and `test/rank/` (each signal on its own), `test/query.test.ts` (words, ranking, the answer reader, determinism, patches, vocabulary changes), `test/fuzz.test.ts` (10,000 seeded random strings in every mode and scope, every answer well formed, no failure caught inside), `test/perf.test.ts` (a made-up corpus of 1,400 static entries, 5,400 ids and 5,000 things; three times the budget on CI), `test/engine-fixtures.ts` (made-up words and household things, no game word); `test/smoke.test.ts` now checks the real engine.
- Measured (`test/perf.test.ts`, Node 24, this container's 4 cores shared at a load of 10 to 25; median of three builds, each with its dictionary and typo index; the smaller of wall and CPU time): static 50 to 104 ms (budget 150), vanilla 61 to 95 ms (250), 5,000 things 63 to 98 ms (150), a patch of 10 things 8 to 15 ms; queries p95 4 to 9 ms static (30), 4 to 16 ms with vanilla (60), 9 to 16 ms with the 5,000 things (60), median 0.5 to 1 ms; memory 10.0 to 10.3 MB with everything, the entries themselves included (12; typed arrays 1.6 MB).
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @msm/search test` (`--maxWorkers=2`), `pnpm lint` (Biome and check-deps), `pnpm typecheck`.

**Decisions**
- Stemming and the vocabulary are applied at query time, never in the index: the index keeps words as they are, a query word reaches every word of its stem class, and a vocabulary change or a new project word never rebuilds a layer; field counts and lengths are kept per posting and entry, so BM25F uses the whole index's statistics and a patched layer answers exactly as a rebuilt one (a test checks it).
- Protected words (B653's note): a protected word that is the plain plural of a dictionary word (`-s`, `-es`, `-ies`) is not protected, so a word and its plural meet; `-ves` words stay protected (B650's `leaves`/`leave`).
- The ideas of D6's fields are reached at query time at 0.85 of the field they land in (0.5 for near words), not stored as a field of the entry.
- Folding is by action descriptor: a tile, a Showcase card and the flow they open fold when the app gives them the same action; a tile with a chooser has its own. The Custom sword starter cannot fold under the Weapon flow by data (different actions): under the make lean a starter weighs 0.9 against a flow's 1.15, and a flow whose answers took the thing's noun gets 1.3 (`makesThing`, from B659's reader).
- Unavailable entries are never Best matches and come last in their section (stricter than "never first while an available one scores within a fifth").
- Scopes filter by section (`mine` keeps Things to fix too); Advanced reads the prefixes `>`, `@`, `#` and `?`; Very easy leans to make, the commands scope to commands, and the host may hand in a lean for its door.
- The confidence floor is B650's (a score of 3 and half the words read without a typo correction, or one corrected word, or a whole id); below it there is no Best match.
- `createSearchIndex` moved from `types.ts` to `query.ts` and `smoke.test.ts` changed with it (the stub test asserted the throw); no interface changed.

**Next**
- B659: implement `SearchAnswerReader` (`src/query.ts`): `skip` for the clause words, `extra` for a behaviour's own flows, `absorbed` word indexes (the ranker counts them matched), `makesThing` when the head noun went into an answer, `behaviourFits`; `ReadQuery.folded` holds corrected words (a multi-word idea in one slot) and `ideas` the vocabulary ideas by word.
- B660: hand in the plugins' vocabularies with `setVocabulary`, the protected words (game id words and headwords) with `setProtected`, the open mod's kinds and templates and the history with `setContext`; call `warm()` after each `setLayer` or `patchLayer` so the key press never builds the dictionary; give a tile, a card and the flow they open the same action descriptor; give Rules entries their catalogue labels as titles (B655); send `toSlim` hits. A vanilla id a target lacks simply matches nothing.
- B666: tune in `rank/weights.ts` only; the B650 misses (Custom sword, vanilla exact titles under the make lean, guide pages against problems) are the first to check.
- Close: `packages/search/CLAUDE.md`'s Status still describes the B652 stub.
## 2026-11-23 — executor — ADR 0126: the Java project generator loaded on first use

**What**
- ADR 0126 (Accepted 2026-11-23, a vetoable default), ADR 0123 D4's follow-up: plugin API **1.24.0** adds `Target.loadJavaProject?(): Promise<JavaProjectGenerator>`, purely additive (`JavaProjectGenerator.generate` stays synchronous, `Target.javaProject` stays, `TargetFacts` has neither; built-ins keep `^1.0.0`). CHANGELOG, `API_VERSION`, package version and the type test updated.
- `packages/targets/mc-26.3/src/target.ts` sets only `loadJavaProject`, a dynamic `import('./java-project/index')`, so the generator is a chunk of its own in the renderer (`assets/java-project-*.js`, 976,443 B) and in main (`java-project-*.js`). `targetFacts` and the app's `toTargetFacts` strip the new hook.
- The `java-project` exporter uses `javaProject` when set, else awaits `loadJavaProject`; a loader that rejects is `export.java-generation-failed` and writes nothing (new exporter test).
- Tests that found the generator through `target.javaProject` read `loadJavaProject` (17 exporter test files, the 26.3 target's tests); the plugins' template tests strip `loadJavaProject` with the other hooks.
- Sizes (Linux, from an empty `app/out`): renderer first paint 5,721,711 B to 4,746,064 B (-975,647 B); renderer total, what `check-size` budgets, 19,370,570 B to 19,371,628 B (18.5 of 19 MB either way: the lazy chunk is counted); main `index.js` 2.5 to 1.3 MB; `app.asar` 27.2 MB both. `check-size` within budget.
- Checks: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, tests of plugin-api (107), core (206), targets all (82), mc-26.3 (267), mc-26.4 (151), exporters (2,001 passed, 139 skipped as before; goldens unchanged), the ten touched plugins and the app (3,435 passed, 1 skipped; `--maxWorkers=2`); `pnpm build`, `dist:dir`, e2e `eject-path` (3 passed, `--trace off`).

**Decisions**
- A new optional hook rather than `generate` returning `MaybePromise`: widening a 1.x member's return narrows what callers may rely on (ADR 0036's policy); the hook is additive.
- Option B (eject in main) not taken: option A keeps the generator out of first paint without IPC.
- `tools/check-size` not changed: no budget loosened; whether it reports or budgets the first-paint set is the orchestrator's call.

**Next**
- Orchestrator: the plans that counted on about 1 MB of room from this follow-up (`PLAN-search.md`, `PLAN-ai-helper-2.md`) get none under the total-based budget; decide whether `check-size` gains a first-paint report or budget (entry script plus its `modulepreload` chunks and CSS from `index.html`) beside the total.
- Root `CLAUDE.md`'s "Plugin API 1.23.0" status line and `docs/HANDOFF.md` name the old version; update at the next handover.

## 2026-11-23 — executor — Molten amber light flake (CI run 45098044992)

**What**
- Cause: `SampleVillagersParityTest.moltenAmberGivesLight` read the block light a fixed 5 ticks after setting the block. The server's light engine (`ThreadedLevelLightEngine`, whose `checkBlock` only queues the work) runs the update later on the shared background workers, which also generate the other tests' chunks, and `getBrightness` reads 0 until it has. The GameTest server does not pace its ticks (0.46 ms a tick at the fastest measured), so 5 ticks is a few milliseconds against work measured in wall time. Neither the ejected code nor the runtime is wrong: the liquid block's emission is 12 in both, and the light is 12 and 11 above once the engine has run.
- Evidence (26.3, temporary probe tests, not committed): light 0 at tick 0 and 12/11 from tick 1 (15 ms) on an idle server, tick 1 (113 to 133 ms) in three full `sample_villagers_*` runs; with the background workers held for 300 ms the old test body failed 3 of 3 with the CI message ("was 0 on tick 5"), the light arriving at tick 315; in a full ejected run on one CPU (`taskset -c 0`) the real test failed with the CI message in 1 of 3 runs while the probe in the same run saw the light arrive at tick 11 (385 ms). In every run the light engine's `waitForPendingTasks` future was done exactly when the numbers were right.
- Fix: the test takes `waitForPendingTasks` for the block's chunk and `succeedWhen` waits for it, then checks 12 and 11; `maxTicks` 6000 (about 3 s of light delay at the fastest tick; a first 1000 was too short with five 300 ms tasks on three workers: 1000 ticks in 0.75 s), with the measured reason in its Javadoc. `SampleModParityTest.skyLightPassesTheRubyGlass` (the only other parity test that reads the light engine) waits the same way for both chunks' futures (before them the cell below the glass reads 15 whatever the glass does), `maxTicks` 100 to 6000.
- Verified: the fixed test with the workers held passed 5 of 5; full `sample_villagers_*` 15 of 15 on the ejected jar 3 times, on the content jar 3 times and on the ejected jar on one CPU 4 times; the ruby glass test 3 times each on the sample mod's ejected and content jars, full `sample_mod_*` 83 of 83 on each; the parity jar builds for 26.3 and 26.4.

**Decisions**
- Waiting on the light engine's own future rather than on the numbers: a wrong light value then fails as a wrong value, not as a slow engine.
- The runtime's own GameTests `MsmFluidGameTest.liquidBlockLight` and `MsmShapeGameTest.skyLightPassesASeeThroughCube` poll with `succeedWhen` at `maxTicks` 100 (about 46 ms at the fastest tick): the same weakness, outside this brief, left for a follow-up.

**Next**
- Give the two runtime GameTests above the same wait (the light engine's future, a budget sized in wall time).

- Today's guide: 39 pages, 569 sections (39 titles, 429 `##`, 60 `###`, 41 `####`), 124 kB as JSON, built in about 45 ms; 39 sections open with a table or code and have no sentence; 25 carry an alias. Every in-guide link to a heading (more than 250) finds an anchor or alias in the index.
- Tests: `app/test/main/vanilla-names.test.ts` (a made-up jar and lang file through extraction: sorts, left-out keys and values, no lang file, a link out of the cache refused, traversal in the version and target id refused, too large and not an object, the IPC handler by target), `app/test/main/guide.test.ts` (a made-up folder: index, anchors and sentences, kept; pages of the list only, `../`, `.md`, other files and missing names refused; a link out of the folder and a too large page refused; both channels through the IPC handlers; the real guide indexed with every heading link resolved; anchors as the docs site and GitHub write them), `app/test/ipc-contract.test.ts` (samples for the three channels, bounds of names and the guide).
- Checks: app tests with `--maxWorkers=2` (3,498 passed, 1 skipped), `pnpm lint` (Biome and check-deps), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, `dist:dir` (`resources/guide/` holds the 39 pages, 880 kB; `app.asar` holds no `.md` file), `node tools/check-size/index.ts`: `app.asar` 27.2 MB of 32, renderer 18.5 MB of 19 (the renderer is not touched by this brief).

**Decisions**
- Potions are carried as an eighth sort (SQ8's route kept their prefix; D3's vanilla layer lists potions); subtitles are keyed by the subtitle key's tail, which is the sound event's path for most sounds but not all (`sounds.json` is not in the cache).
- The guide service is built in `registerIpc` from Electron's `app`, and `createIpcHandlers` takes it as an optional last argument, so `node-platform.ts` and `index.ts` (where other briefs work) are not touched.
- `####` headings are indexed with level 4 (the guide links to some); the search may weigh or leave them out by level.

**Next**
- B660: `vanilla-names.ts` in the renderer caches `platform.minecraft.readNames?.(targetId)` per target (null or an error: names from the ids); a block's item key is often missing (the item takes its block's name). Guide entries from `platform.guide?.index()`: `level` 1 is the page, `sentence` may be empty, and `tokenise`/`fold` run there.
- B661: open a page with `platform.guide.page(name)`; resolve `name.md#x` and `#x` links against `anchor` or `alias` of the index (or the same two slug functions, `guideAnchor` and `githubAnchor` in `app/src/main/guide.ts`, mirrored in the renderer).
- B662: nothing from this brief.
- Main session: the channel list in `app/CLAUDE.md` (`minecraft:names`, `guide:index|page`, `resources/guide/`).

## 2026-11-23 — executor — Runtime light GameTests wait for the light engine

**What**
- The follow-up of the molten amber light flake (84ecab7): the runtime's own `MsmFluidGameTest.liquidBlockLight` and `MsmShapeGameTest.skyLightPassesASeeThroughCube` polled the light with `succeedWhen` at `maxTicks` 100, which on the unpaced GameTest server (about 0.5 ms a tick) is tens of milliseconds against light work that the server's light engine runs later, in wall time, on the shared background workers. Both now take the light engine's `waitForPendingTasks` futures for the chunks of the blocks they set, fail each poll until those are done, then check the values; `maxTicks` 6000.
- New package-private helper `engine-mod/src/gametest/.../gametest/LightWait.java` (`queued(helper, positions...)`, `assertRun`, `MAX_TICKS` 6000) with the measured reason in its Javadoc; the two tests' Javadocs say why.
- Searched the gametest sources for every other light read: `MsmGrowingPlantGameTest` reads `getMaxLocalRawBrightness` only for a failure message; `MsmPlants3ClientGameTest` and `MsmVanillaBlocksClientGameTest` read the client level's light, which the client works through on its own paced ticks, with `waitFor` timeouts; none has this weakness, none changed.
- Evidence (temporary probe tests and a temporary filter property, not committed; the probe ran the old and the new forms side by side, with the background workers held by `2 x maxAllowedExecutorThreads + 1` tasks of 300 ms or not, filtered run of five tests on a fresh server, 4 CPUs): 26.3, the values arrived at tick 236 (641 ms) even unheld and at ticks 1327 to 1338 (about 1.8 s) held, so the old 100-tick form failed in 4 of 4 and the new form passed in 4 of 4; 26.4, unheld at tick 9 (28 ms, old form passes), held at tick 3247 (1.87 s, 0.57 ms a tick), old form failed 3 of 3, new form passed. A probe expecting a wrong value (8 for the custom liquid's 9) failed on 26.3 as "Expected ... to be 8: was 9", not as a slow light engine (on 26.4 it ran out of its own short 200-tick limit with the workers still held).
- `./gradlew build` passed for `-Pmc=26.3` and `-Pmc=26.4`: 851 of 851 required GameTests each, the shape test logging 15 below the cube and 14 below stone.

**Decisions**
- One shared helper rather than a copy per test, matching the parity mod's form (future first, then the values, so a wrong value fails as a wrong value).

**Next**
- None for this flake; if another light test is added to the runtime GameTests, use `LightWait`.
